## Gotchas

- **Verify image dimensions match the target use before claiming done.** Social cards (1200x630, usually built by the site from the post's largest image), blog headers, and listing thumbnails (512 wide) have different size requirements. A header that works on the blog may be too small to build a sharp OG/social card.
- **When asked to use a specific image URL or file, use exactly that asset.** Don't substitute similar images. Past rating-1 failures came from using wrong image assets.
- **`--remove-bg` may produce black backgrounds instead of transparency.** Verify transparent PNG output visually before deploying.
- **`RemoveBg.ts` converts in place and zeroes RGB under removed alpha, so the original is unrecoverable.** Running it on a `.jpg` replaces the file with the cut `.png`; if rembg eats an element (paper stacks, thin props, the DA-name signature), you cannot flatten the alpha back to recover the source and must regenerate (cost: a full new roll, 2026-08-16). `cp` the original before running RemoveBg.ts on a one-of-a-kind generation, every time.
- **`--thumbnail` / `--remove-bg` can erase whole subjects in multi-subject compositions (2026-09-23, a two-subject blog header).** rembg's default model keeps only the most salient object and fades the rest; on a two-ecosystem scene it kept one hub and fogged out the rival network and the person, and because the raw is deleted and RGB is zeroed under removed alpha the loss was unrecoverable. For any composition with more than one subject, keep the raw (copy it, or point `REMBG_BIN` at a wrapper that saves it first) and cut with `rembg -m birefnet-general`, which kept every element with a clean edge. Read the cut PNG and confirm every subject survived before judging it.
- **`--remove-bg` is unsafe for thin-linework technical diagrams.** rembg classifies thin black ink on a light field as "background" and strips it, leaving a near-empty ghost. Documented 2026-05-11 on a flowchart. Mitigations: (a) prompt for *thick* saturated linework first so rembg has a strong signal, or (b) skip `--remove-bg` entirely when the destination background matches the image's background (an opaque diagram drawn on the page's own ground, `PREFERENCES.md` § Color palette, composites with zero visible seam, no alpha needed).
- **Logo fidelity breaks in 3D/perspective scenes even with a reference image.** Documented 2026-06-11 on a brand wallpaper set: straight-on and macro scenes held the glyph topology, but the isometric 3D scene changed it (an open stroke closed, a separate element dropped). For any perspective/3D composition with a logo, add topology-locked negative language to the prompt that names each feature of the mark ("do not close the open stroke", "do not omit the separate element", name every stroke and terminal) on top of `--reference-image`, and vision-verify the topology specifically. The install mark and its topology rules live in `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Art/PREFERENCES.md` § Wallpaper.
- **nano-banana-pro "4K 16:9" is actually 5504×3072 (43:24, ~0.8% wider than 16:9), saved as .jpg even when `--output` says .png.** Disclose the native ratio when the spec says 16:9, and probe the real filename before Read/delivery.
- **Image models default every person to white, so every figure treatment is stated in the prompt (principal, 2026-07-12, 2026-09-20, 2026-09-23).** `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Art/PREFERENCES.md` § Character design sets the treatment and the sentence the prompts carry; without it the skill default is a varied cast whose skin tone, age and build each prompt names, spanning a natural range. Any multi-figure scene (essay headers, comics, visualizations) states the treatment explicitly, a group that defaults to one ethnicity is a hard failure, and the ArtDirection rubric scores a violation as a critical defect. See Essay.md HUMAN FIGURES block + Step 8 checklist.
- **Every art request uses its matching intent and that intent's technique, plus `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Art/PREFERENCES.md` when present, unless the principal names a different style (principal, 2026-09-24).** Feedback about tone ("more positive", "less dark") is fixed inside the technique: lighter ground, warmer washes, smaller cool accent, a different scene. It is never a license to switch medium. A "more positive" redo once went out in a different painted medium under `--intent=Essay` and was rejected. The Essay contract's `mandates` and medium bans now refuse that prompt in `Generate.ts`.
- **Essay/blog headers are signed with the DA name (`getDAName()` from `hooks/lib/identity`; principal, 2026-06-20 + 2026-07-09) in a small, integrated cursive signature hand.** `Generate.ts` stamps it programmatically (Essay.md Step 7.1: the macOS cursive `SignPainter-HouseScript` face by default, ~3% of image width, semi-transparent charcoal, slight rotation, tucked into the composition's bottom-right); never prompt the signature into the model, because it garbles. A large print-letter signature reads as a label rather than a painter's mark; faces the principal has rejected for the signature are listed in `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Art/PREFERENCES.md` § Signature.
- Kept inline: the frontmatter eval contract, the four safety gates (intent gate, output staging, quality loop, vendors), the default Generate.ts command, and the cross-intent gotchas that RemoveBackground, TechnicalDiagrams, Comics, Visualize, Mermaid, Comparisons and the wallpaper intents point at as "SKILL.md Gotchas"; every run needs them.
- **Image generation is Google plus Flux, never OpenAI** — Nano Banana Pro (the default) and Nano Banana from Google, plus Flux; the last two run on Replicate. OpenAI image models are not used. Image skills and intents must not offer an OpenAI image option, and requests for one should error and point to Nano Banana Pro. <!-- applied: 2026-10-13T08:59:41.378Z -->

# ArtDirection

A shared quality loop for artistic deliverables: the Brief defines audience, register, references and bar; a Direction council resolves the visual intent into `Direction.md`; the domain skill produces the artifact against it; Critique yields two vendors' scores and ranked defects; iteration reaches the bar or reports the shortfall at four rounds; only a passing result reaches Deliver; and Calibrate records the principal's own verdict as evidence for later judge calibration. The domain skill makes the artifact; this skill supplies the quality evidence.

## Ideal State

- Nothing artistic reaches the principal or a public surface without a current passing critique from the judge panel bound to the exact bytes delivered. The panel is cross-vendor whenever two approved vendors are reachable; a one-vendor panel may still pass, and its report carries the `vendor_missing` flag as weaker evidence.
- Every verdict is honest: pass only when the pooled median reaches the bar and each vendor median reaches bar minus 0.5, with no UNKNOWN score or critical defect, a cap hit reported with its shortfall, and an unreachable vendor reported as unavailable rather than as a quality failure.
- Each round names ranked, located defects a producer can fix, judged against the concept-first rubric rather than adjectives.
- A figure's anatomy and mechanics are judged as a defect class: extra or missing limbs, a grip or pose that does not match the object held, or physically impossible motion is a critical defect located by image region or frame, so the critique fails it; the judges read this rule from `References/Rubric.md`.
- The principal's own scores are kept verbatim as labels, and judges change only through a deliberate calibration, never automatically.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Loop** | Full quality loop or iterate to the bar | `Intents/Loop.md` |
| **Direction** | Art council or new visual direction | `Intents/Direction.md` |
| **Critique** | Rate the visuals or inspect a render | `Intents/Critique.md` |
| **Deliver** | Hand over a passing artifact | `Intents/Deliver.md` |
| **Calibrate** | Record the principal's score and note | `Intents/Calibrate.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `References/Rubric.md` | writing a brief or reading a critique: the anchored axes, document and figure rules, defect shape and the `Brief.json` schema (`References/BriefExample.json` is a filled brief); Critique reads it at runtime |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: the two judge vendors' access, ffmpeg for films, and a no-cost proof |

## Tool contract

Run with `bun skills/ArtDirection/` prefixed to each tool path, from the config root.

| Tool | CLI contract |
|---|---|
| Critique | `Tools/Critique.ts --video <mp4> \| --image <png> [--images <glob>] --brief <Brief.json> [--bar 8.5] [--samples 12] [--concurrency N] [--vendors openai,anthropic] [--sample-seed <n>] [--out <dir>] [--json] [--allow-identity]` |
| Deliver | `Tools/Deliver.ts --artifact <file> [--critique <Critique.json>] --to <dir>` |
| Calibrate | `Tools/Calibrate.ts --artifact <file> --verdict <1-10> --note "<text>"` |

Each intent file carries its tool's defaults, refusals and exit codes.

## Data & Config

User customizations live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/ArtDirection/` (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When it exists, its PREFERENCES.md, configurations and resources override the defaults here; when absent, the defaults stand. First-time setup (accounts, keys, config, a proof it works) is in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

- A brief may name `"calibration": "<target>"`. Critique then adds that Calibrate target's `Taste.json` (the principal's labeled likes and dislikes) to the judge prompt and records its `labels_hash` in the report; a target with no profile yet is noted under `outstanding`. Briefs without the field produce the prompt they always did.
- Calibration labels append to `~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/ArtDirection/labels.jsonl` (fields in `Intents/Calibrate.md`).
- The panel is the vision vendors named by `art_judges` in `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/ArtDirection/Config.md` (OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have seats; a missing file or key stops the critique with an error naming both). That folder's `PREFERENCES.md`, when present, is appended to `References/Rubric.md` as install-specific judging rules, and `check_set.version` hashes the two together. OpenAI vision runs as `codex exec -i` through the codex CLI signed in to ChatGPT (`Assay/Tools/OpenAIVision.ts`; no API key is read); Anthropic vision runs through `LIFEOS/TOOLS/Inference.ts` image input (the claude CLI on the subscription), never falling back to another vendor. Panel selection (`--vendors`) is in `Intents/Critique.md`. No credentials belong in briefs or logs.
- Models come from `LIFEOS/TOOLS/models.ts`: `CROSS_VENDOR.openaiJudge` for OpenAI and the high rung of `EFFORT_MODEL` for Anthropic, never pinned here.
- Preferences use configRoot above; the current credential and label implementations use the home `.claude` location.

## Gotchas

- Hand-over is gated by `Deliver.ts` because a first-draft video reached the principal with no critique on 2026-09-17, while the rule lived only in prose (the story is in the USER extension's `History.md`).
- The rubric leads with `concept` (does the artifact carry its idea as one metaphor a stranger reads at a glance), and overall follows concept most. Changed 2026-09-28 after the principal's first Calibrate scores showed the old craft-first rubric ranking the scored artifacts almost at random (the measurement is in the USER extension's `History.md`).

## Examples

User: "iterate until it's great" on a render → Loop intent → `Brief.json` and `Direction.md` exist, critique rounds run until the artifact passes the bar, or the four-round cap is reported with its shortfall.

User: "rate the visuals" → Critique intent → `Critique.json` with both vendors' scores, ranked defects and a pass, fail or unavailable verdict.

User: "that one's a 6, the type is cramped" → Calibrate intent → one label appended with verdict 6 and the note in the principal's words.

# Assay — Assertion-First AI Evaluation

**Contents:** Ideal State · Intent Routing · The taxonomy · Choosing a check: tier first, then shape · Selection, acceptance, and unavailable evidence · The canonical path · Doctrine (from Anthropic; encode, don't restate) · The image lane (visual evals) · Harness integration · Judgment-layer question systems · Data & Config · Gotchas · Examples

An eval gives an AI an input, then applies **assertions** to its output to measure success (Anthropic's definition). A case is `{id, prompt, assert:[...]}`. Each assertion is either deterministic (code, free) or model-graded (a calibrated judge). Cases run multiple trials and report **pass^k** (every trial passes; the reliability metric and the regression gate) and **pass@k** (any trial passes). Proof applies the same tiers to one run's output (the film, image, page, email or document it made) against what was asked, before the principal sees it: `Intents/Proof.md`, with the whole system in `LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Assay/AssaySystem.md`. CreateQuestions designs the fast tier itself: it turns a fuzzy decision into a measured judgment-layer question system (`LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Assay/AssaySystem.md` § Judgment layer).

Sources: [Demystifying evals for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents) (2026-01), [A Statistical Approach to Model Evaluations](https://www.anthropic.com/research/statistical-approach-to-model-evals) (2024-11), [develop tests](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/build-with-claude/develop-tests), the eval-awareness contamination post (2026-03), and the live `claude plugin eval` surface.

**Freshness contract:** "aligned to Anthropic's doctrine" is a live claim. When designing a new suite class or touching `## Doctrine`, re-fetch the demystifying-evals post and flag where it has moved. Report divergence, never auto-adopt; an unreachable URL never blocks a run.

## Ideal State

- Every check sits at the lowest tier that can honestly answer it (code, glance, judge, human), and only code runs on a blocking path.
- Every score ships with pass^k, SEM and a 95% CI from the trials that completed, with the requested and completed trial counts beside it; fewer completed trials than requested never claims pass^k.
- A judged check is calibrated against the principal's labels or reads PROVISIONAL wherever it shows, and a judged suite keeps an adversarial fixture its judge must fail.
- A produced artifact is checked by Proof against what was asked before the principal sees it, and the receipt is bound to its bytes.
- Transport failures, malformed verdicts and missing observations are reported as unavailable evidence, never as a pass, a quality failure or an adversarial catch.
- A fuzzy decision handed to CreateQuestions leaves as a validated question system whose accuracy was measured on held-out cases the designer never saw, with its margin over one holistic baseline question, or as a stated finding that the judgment layer does not fit and what does; a design ends at a saved shadow registry row and never moves a caller toward enforce.
- When Assay builds the eval system for a project, the project's ISA ends current: every criterion it checks names its suite or glance question in Test Strategy, and the hand-rolled eval code, rows and stale criteria it replaced are removed in the same change.

## The taxonomy

`eval` is the parent word for every check a criterion carries. Its two branches are the **assert** (a tool says no: `Assertions.ts`, `bun test`, a curl probe) and the **judged** check (a model or Assay's judgment layer says no, bound to content derived from the ideal state). A judged check takes one of three harness shapes: a **glance** row (one typed question to the judgment layer over state that already exists), a **rubric** run from an `eval` suite (`Judge.ts`, one output scored against anchored levels), or a **tournament** on a `pairwise` row (`Tournament.ts`, every pair judged in both orders, then a shuffled-seed rerun). `manual` is not a class; it is the top of the ladder below, and every attestation the principal gives is a label for the rung beneath it. What makes a judge good is its content, derived from the ISA's articulated ideal state. The same words appear in ISAFormat § *Verifier classes, lanes, and stages*, TestingDoctrine, the Bunker doc, the Algorithm, and the ISA skill; change them everywhere or nowhere.

**The four-tier ladder.** Every check sits on one of four tiers, ordered by speed and by how much intelligence the verifier needs: `code`, `glance`, `judge`, `human`. Code is a tool that exits zero. The `glance` tier is one typed question to Assay's judgment layer, answered with a probability, far faster than a model judge (the sub-second figure was measured on the engine retired 2026-10-10 and not re-measured; `skills/Assay/References/QuestionDesign.md`). Judge is a model reading an output against anchored levels or a flipped bracket, in seconds to minutes. Human is the principal recognizing the thing on encounter. The tier is derived from the row's `type` and is never authored: the deterministic types give `code`, a `glance` row gives `glance`, `eval` and `pairwise` give `judge`, and `manual` gives `human`. A check sits at the lowest tier that can honestly answer it, and it drifts down the ladder as it earns labels: a human row becomes a `glance` row once the criterion carries labels, and a `glance` row becomes a code row once the question is sharp enough to be a tool. Two guards hold this in place. Only code runs on the blocking path, so no `glance`, `eval`, or `pairwise` row runs on the liveness lane or inside a deploy or close gate, and a judged row never gates a deterministic row of the same criterion. A gate runs no judge, but it reads recorded results: an earned judged row's latest fail keeps the criterion open at close. Every Feature also keeps at least one spanning criterion over the whole artifact at the consumer boundary, and the maintainer-side `bunker test --tiers` flags a Feature whose leaves are all `glance` rows as `unspanned`. The `glance` row contract is fixed: type `glance`, a tool cell of the form `glance:<question-file>#<question-id>`, and a JSON question file beside the ISA under `Questions/`. That file carries one typed question and a bounded producer command that emits the structured state to judge. The registry threshold means confidence for every question type, so a noul resolves two-sided and carries a verdict plus the confidence behind it. A row under a shadow caller reports `shadow`, its own status, which counts as neither a pass nor a fail and cannot close a criterion. Every verdict records the sha256 of the artifact it judged, and the call is skipped when the artifact hash, the question, the threshold, and the engine model are all unchanged since the last verdict. Labels that came from a model or from the deterministic layer put the calibration record in the `proxy` state, which never reads earned.

## Choosing a check: tier first, then shape

Tier first. If code can answer, write the assert and stop. If reading is needed and the state already exists (a file, a rendered page, a diff, a log tail, a query result), write a `glance` row that asks one typed question about it. If the output is generated fresh on every trial (a prompt's answer, an agent's run), write an `eval` suite, because pass^k needs trials and the judgment layer cannot generate. A `manual` row holds taste until labels exist.

Shape second, for anything that has to be read. Every engine answer is a probability, so the probability is not what separates the shapes. The question type is, and each one becomes a different piece of code:

| Question | Shape | What the code does with it | Where it lives here |
|---|---|---|---|
| Is this true? | `noul` | an `if` | `llm-assert` in a suite; `kind: noul` in a question file |
| Which of these? (an unordered set) | `choice` | a `switch` | `kind: choice` in a question file; A/B/tie inside a tournament |
| How much? (an ordered ladder) | `score` | a sort, or a threshold | anchored `llm-rubric` in a suite; `kind: score` in a question file |

Critical, high, medium, low is a ladder and can be sorted. Korean, Mexican, Thai cannot, so a question over them is a choice. Ask many small questions rather than one big rubric. A rubric whose levels mix dimensions is several questions crushed into one call, the same failure as a system message packed with instructions in the hope that every one lands. Fall back to a multi-level anchored rubric or a tournament only when the property will not split.

An unearned judgment only flags; an earned confident no fails like a code check. In `Judge.ts` an `llm-assert` goes to the judgment layer as a noul and an anchored `llm-rubric` as a score before any model judge is paid for. A confident answer from a caller in enforce mode resolves the assert, the middle band escalates to the model judge as UNKNOWN, and an unanchored rubric never reaches the engine (it escalates and counts as residue with reason `unanchored`). The full escalation rule is in `References/Progressive.md`.

On the maintainer install a judged miss is one command (the Bunker CLI is maintainer-private and not in the public release; a public install calibrates through a suite with a judged assert and `Tools/Calibrate.ts`). `bunker miss` adds the missing question to the criterion's question file, registers it in shadow, and keeps the state as a labelled case, so the fix is one more question and a kept case rather than a longer prompt. `bunker label` adds a labelled case to a question that exists; `bunker attest` labels a `manual` row. Commands and flags: `Intents/Calibrate.md` § Tool contract, The miss loop.

## Selection, acceptance, and unavailable evidence

A tournament answers which candidate is preferred under a written definition. It never proves the winner meets an absolute bar. A quality criterion carries its own asserts and rubric, or a named principal attestation when calibration is unavailable. Both definitions derive from the owning ISA; neither the word "best" nor a number supplies the standard.

`Tournament.ts` needs at least two distinct candidates and a completed shuffled rerun to verify; `--no-rerun` is diagnostic only. Identical content under different paths is not candidate diversity.

Semantic UNKNOWN stays a miss even under negation. Unavailable evidence and trial counts follow the Ideal State above.

## Doctrine (from Anthropic; encode, don't restate)

- Deterministic first; judges are debt. "Prefer deterministic graders where possible, use LLM graders where necessary." Every judged assert carries a retirement plan: calibration against principal labels, disagreements mined into deterministic asserts, and a per-suite judged residue reported every run and expected to fall. (Shrinkage doctrine: principal directive 2026-08-25.)
- Grade outcomes, not paths. Agents find valid approaches designers did not anticipate. Transcript analysis is for quality signals only, never pass/fail.
- Capability suites start low and graduate; regression suites target ~100% and gate on pass^k. SuiteManager tracks saturation.
- Statistics or it didn't happen. Every score ships with SEM and a 95% CI, never a bare mean; comparisons are paired-difference only; null results check power first; clustered cases use clustered SEs.
- Judge discipline: the judge is never the generator, one dimension per judge, anchored scales, reason before score, UNKNOWN is a miss, and a suite earns the cheap judge only on an EARNED record (thresholds in the Calibrate.ts row above; authoring rules in CreateJudge). Raw agreement alone rewards a constant judge on a skewed set, which is why each class needs its own labels at better-than-coin agreement.
- A judged suite with no earned record is PROVISIONAL and says so everywhere. EvalRunner's report carries `provisional`, its age in days, and the reason; the maintainer-side `bunker test` prints `PROVISIONAL (Nd: reason)`; Pulse shows an amber pill, red past 30 days; a Socrates standing question asks daily whether any judged suite runs uncalibrated. Nothing blocks, but the count stays in sight.
- Eval integrity is adversarial (contamination post, 2026-03). Never publish suite cases as examples; identity-bound suites stay in the USER layer; assume anything published is trained on.
- Never trust a score until you read the transcripts. Every run persists them to `MEMORY/STATE/Evals-Results/<suite>/<run>/run.json`.

## The image lane (visual evals)

Suite-scoped rubric provider selection, private-image consent, capability probes and failure behavior follow [Vision judge providers](References/VisionJudgeProviders.md). The default rubric judge is the OpenAI + Anthropic panel (see Gotchas); any other provider requires its own current calibration. Image cases share the text runner's prerequisite contract (see Gotchas), and a skipped judgment can never count as catching an adversarial fixture.

Images are graded, never generated, by `Tools/ImageEvalRunner.ts -s <suite>` over the same suite roots and result shape as text. Deterministic layer (`Tools/ImageAsserts.ts`, magick + tesseract, local, no egress): dimensions, aspect, format, max-bytes, luminance bands (dark-ground rule), `ocr-contains`, and `ocr-word-ratio`, the mechanical garbled-text catch. Judged layer (`Tools/VisionJudge.ts`, the OpenAI + Anthropic panel by default; Gemini only when a suite's config entry names Google, on `--public`, or for pairwise): anchored `vision-rubric` asserts (trials apply to judged asserts only; deterministic image checks run once), a `pairwise` CLI for which-of-two verdicts (Gemini only; see Gotchas), and the meaning ladder (`meaning-ladder` asserts; `VisionJudge.ts describe` then `ladder`). The ladder's blind describer sees the image and nothing else (no article, thesis, or title); a text judge then grades the description against the case's `reference:` argument summary on four anchored rungs (unrelated · topic only · argument · specific claim) and never sees the image. Worked example: Art Essay Step 8 (assert gate → blind describer → meaning ladder → flipped `Tournament.ts`), suite `art-meaning-recovery`. A result records generator, describer, and judge ids and flags a same-family pair.

Identity guard: images carrying the principal's likeness are not sent to the vision judge pending explicit clearance. VisionJudge refuses `/headshot/i` paths without `--allow-identity`, suites default `allow_identity: false`, and deterministic asserts remain available for everything. Taste guard: pure-taste dimensions ride pairwise plus principal ratification, never absolute auto-grades.

## Harness integration

- Config-change regression: run `bun LIFEOS/TOOLS/ConfigEvalOnChange.ts` by hand to execute the configured dispositions suite after a behaviour-defining file changes (default `core-dispositions`; override via `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Assay/config.json` `config_change_suite`).
- ISA and Algorithm: every ISC carries an executable check as a Test Strategy row that Assay resolves at the cheapest honest tier (code assert, then the judgment layer, then a model judge, then the principal); the maintainer-side `bunker test` row engine executes those rows (a public install runs code rows with `bun test ./<path>` and suite rows with `Tools/EvalRunner.ts`), and Development Test and the post-deploy probes call it. A row typed `eval` with a `suite:` dispatches to EvalRunner and its pass^k verdict is the criterion's evidence; `pairwise` dispatches to `Tournament.ts` and its stable winner is the evidence; `glance` stays in the Bunker runner and never enters this skill's runner. A per-ISC `eval` row is required for behavioral, quality, and regression criteria; a separate second-look suite stays elective. Judged rows default to stage 2, so the criterion's asserts run first and a failing one gates the judge; a gated row is never dispatched and never a pass (ISAFormat v2.27.0).
- USER layer: identity-bound suites live in `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Assay/Suites/`, calibration sets in `.../Calibration/`, never in the public tree.

## Judgment-layer question systems

The runtime is `LIFEOS/ASSAY/`. Status, reports and tuning need no intent; they are direct commands on `Assay.ts`. A readiness question ("is this caller ready to enforce?") is answered from `tune` and `report`, with balanced accuracy, label counts and each blocker by name.

| Command | Answers |
|---|---|
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts status` | every caller's mode, rows and error rate, and whether agreement is computable; exits 1 when an enforced question is under its label floor or rests on proxy ground truth |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts report --caller <name> [--days N]` | agreement, balanced accuracy and separation per question against the caller's ground truth |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts tune --caller <name> [--days N] [--step S] [--json]` | threshold sweep, recommended thresholds, and what blocks enforce |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts alerts` | any caller whose error rate is over its floor (exit 1) |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts drift` | enforce rows reverted because the engine's model changed |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts callers [--check-docs]` | the registry, and with `--check-docs` any caller missing its Router data-class row |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts ask --state <text> --questions <json> [--caller name]` | one ad-hoc call |
| `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts ask-many --states <jsonl> --questions <json> [--caller name] [--concurrency N]` | the same questions over many states, as a pool |

The question-system tool is `bun LIFEOS/ASSAY/QuestionSystem.ts validate | cases | run | registry-row`; its contract and flags are in `Intents/CreateQuestions.md` § Tools.

## Data & Config

Before executing, check `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Assay/` (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`) and apply any PREFERENCES.md and `config.json` found there; identity-bound suites and calibration sets live there too (Harness integration). If the directory does not exist, use the skill defaults. First-time setup (accounts, keys, config, a proof it works) is in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

## Gotchas

- Frequent liveness probes run with `LIFEOS_INFERENCE_DISABLED`; both the shared text inference path and the vision judge refuse calls under that flag before loading credentials or contacting a provider.
- A lane-liveness suite needs its own `system_prompt`. Under the live DA prompt the assistant treats "reply with exactly one word" as a constitutional format conflict and refuses (Bunker `bunker-eval-lane`, 2026-09-03), a real answer to the wrong question. Suites that test plumbing rather than behavior set a minimal echo `system_prompt`.
- The single-shot agent under test narrates tool calls. EvalRunner injects an `[EVALUATION CONTEXT] no tools, answer directly` suffix; keep it when authoring output-graded cases. Tool-dependent properties belong in RunAgentic.
- The judge default is dynamic. No judge keys in the suite → the level measured by its current EARNED calibration record, else 'high'. Explicit `judge_model`/`judge_level` always wins. A model bump, rubric edit or label edit makes the old record provisional until Calibrate re-runs; earning at medium or high never certifies low.
- Regression pass/fail changed at v2.0.0: the gate is pass^k ≥ threshold (was mean ≥ threshold). Historical `passed` values are not comparable across the boundary.
- A judged suite keeps an adversarial fixture, and the runner grades it every run. Text: `adversarial_output:` on a case, a canned output that passes every deterministic assert on that case; the judge must fail it or the suite fails (`adversarial.missed` in the result). Image: a case with `expect: fail`, an unrelated image that passes the deterministic asserts and must land below the judged threshold. `SuiteManager.ts validate` rejects a judged suite with neither, and rejects a fixture that fails its own deterministic asserts. Without one, a green suite proves nothing about the judge.
- An `llm-rubric` reaches the judgment layer only when every level from 1 to `scale` has an anchor; a partial set such as 1/3/5 reads `unanchored` and goes straight to the model judge (`rubricToScoreQuestion`). Which rubrics reached the judgment layer is each run's `jev.escalate_reason`, a stored field named for the engine retired 2026-10-10 (RunEval § Output format).
- Order matters to a pairwise judge. `judgeTextPairwise` and `VisionJudge pairwise` judge one ordering; only `Tournament.ts` flips. A single unflipped pairwise call is a position-bias measurement, not a preference.
- Deterministic asserts are prerequisites, for text and image alike. They default to `required: true`, run before any judge whatever the YAML order, and a failure skips the judges and zeroes the trial. Suites that relied on deterministic partial credit must opt in with `required: false`, and their scores before and after that change are two series. `is-json` checks the whole output; `contains-json` checks an embedded fragment.
- A judge, rubric, or anchor edit breaks score comparability. Recalibrate and treat the trend as two series.
- `claude plugin eval` is a newer Claude Code command whose flags and schema can change between releases. Wrap it, never bind our suite format to its schema, and re-probe `--help` before relying on flags.
- Legacy v1 suites (`tasks:` format) are diagnosed, not run. EvalRunner returns a named error result so callers (ConfigEvalOnChange) degrade loudly, never silently.
- Image suites with no entry in `USER/CONFIG/vision-judge.json` are judged by the OpenAI + Anthropic panel: both vendors judge each trial, it passes only when both pass, the score is the lower, and a missing vendor gives no verdict. Google is never the default seat; a suite reaches Google only when its config entry names it. The install's provider rulings and their history are in `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Assay/PREFERENCES.md`.
- A perfect dev number after question iteration is a warning, not a result. A CreateQuestions pilot reached a perfect dev score while its holdout landed below both the bar and the baseline question. Only the holdout number and the judged-only margin decide anything, and holdout runs once.
- `decide()` is two-sided: it returns `act: true` for a confident no as well as a confident yes, so a consumer always reads `verdict` before acting. `Chain.ts` `keepWhere` and `judgeThenEscalate` treat only a confident yes as actionable and send a confident no to drop or escalate; a system whose confident no is an answer composes through the policy evaluator (`LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts`, `LIFEOS/ASSAY/Chain.ts`, read 2026-09-28).
- A new judgment caller needs a row in `LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Router/RouterSystem.md` § Data class per caller, or `Assay.ts callers --check-docs` names it as a missing doc row and exits 1 (`LIFEOS/ASSAY/Assay.ts`, 2026-09-28).
- `bun test` with a bare relative path silently drops every child process's stdout and stderr in Bun 1.3.6, so spawn-based tests fail with empty output. Always prefix the path with `./` (observed 2026-09-11).
- Image tournaments and `VisionJudge.ts pairwise` judge on Gemini alone (`judgeImagePairwise` in `Tools/VisionJudge.ts`), private material included. Whether private material may go to Google is decided by the shared egress check (`LIFEOS/TOOLS/lib/EvaluatorEgress.ts`, its approved-vendor set); when that set excludes Google, every private image tournament exits 2 verifier unavailable. The install's provider rulings and their dates are in `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Assay/PREFERENCES.md` § Judge providers. A pairwise run needs `GOOGLE_API_KEY`; without it the tournament exits 2 (read in code 2026-10-13).

## Examples

**Example 1: Check a produced artifact before handing it over**
```
User: "proof this film against the brief"
→ Proof intent
→ Proof.ts run --artifact film.mp4 --ask brief.md --destination handoff
→ a receipt bound to the film's sha256, with each code fail, flag and unavailable check listed
```

**Example 2: Ask whether a judge can be trusted**
```
User: "is the art-meaning judge any good?"
→ Calibrate intent
→ Calibrate.ts against the principal's labels for that suite
→ an earned, proxy or stale record with agreement per class and the label count against the floor
```

**Example 3: Turn a fuzzy call into judgment-layer questions**
```
User: "turn this inbox triage call into a question system"
→ CreateQuestions intent
→ QuestionSystem.ts validate, then run on dev and once on holdout against one holistic baseline question
→ holdout accuracy, the margin over the baseline, and a saved shadow registry row
```

description: Cleans spoken audio via Whisper transcription, Claude segment classification, and ffmpeg cuts, plus breath taming and noise-gate artifact repair. USE WHEN clean audio, edit audio, remove filler words, clean podcast, remove ums, cut dead air, polish audio, trim recording, cut stutters, ticking audio, clicking audio, audio clicks, gate artifacts, popping audio, loud breaths, breathing sounds, mouth sounds, mouth clicks, lip smacks, tame the breaths. NOT FOR video composition (HyperFrames) or tight-cutting a podcast or spoken recording for publishing (the video skill's TightCut intent (maintainer-side; not in the public release)).
---

# AudioEditor

Cleans recorded audio automatically: strips filler words, false starts, stutters, spoken edit markers and dead air, and crossfades every cut. Transcribe gets word-level timestamps from Whisper (insanely-fast-whisper on MPS), Analyze has Claude classify each segment (KEEP, CUT_FILLER, CUT_FALSE_START, CUT_EDIT_MARKER, CUT_STUTTER, CUT_DEAD_AIR), telling rhetorical emphasis apart from accidental repetition, and Edit executes the cuts with ffmpeg using 40ms qsin crossfades at every edit point and extracted room tone to fill gaps. An optional Cleanvoice pass removes mouth sounds and remaining fillers and normalizes loudness. Output is cleaned MP3/WAV. Modes: --preview, --aggressive, --polish. BreathTame, LoudnessLock, GateScan and GateRepair handle breaths, delivery loudness and noise-gate ticks on their own.

## Ideal State

- Every output keeps what the speaker meant, their deliberate pauses and natural breathing included, and no edit can be heard.
- Done means heard: a clean scan or a zero exit code never counts on its own.
- Repairs are minimal-touch: each tool changes only the defect it targets and leaves the rest of the audio alone.
- Nothing is changed or uploaded without the user's say: previews modify nothing, ambiguous file matches are asked about, and cloud polish runs only on request.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Clean** | "clean audio", "edit audio", "remove filler words", "clean podcast", "remove ums", "cut dead air", "polish audio" | `Intents/Clean.md` |

Standalone breath, mouth-click, gate-tick and loudness requests ("ticking audio", "gate artifacts", "loud breaths", "mouth clicks", "tame the breaths") also route to Clean, using the Tools table and Gate Artifacts below.

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Tools/` | each tool's `<Name>.help.md` holds its full flags and exit codes |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: ffmpeg and Whisper to install, the optional Cleanvoice key, and a synthesized-tone proof |

## Data & Config

User customizations live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/AudioEditor/` (`configRoot` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When that directory exists, its PREFERENCES.md, configurations and resources apply and override the defaults here; when it is absent, the defaults stand. First-time setup (accounts, keys, config, a proof it works) is in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

## Tools

| Tool | Command | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| **Transcribe** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/Transcribe.ts <file>` | Word-level transcription via Whisper |
| **Analyze** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/Analyze.ts <transcript.json>` | LLM-powered edit classification |
| **Edit** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/Edit.ts <file> <edits.json>` | Execute cuts with crossfades + room tone |
| **Polish** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/Polish.ts <file>` | Cleanvoice API cloud polish |
| **Pipeline** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/Pipeline.ts <file> [--polish]` | Full end-to-end pipeline |
| **GateScan** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/GateScan.ts <file> [--json]` | Detect noise-gate ticking (silence-boundary steps); exit 1 on defects |
| **GateRepair** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/GateRepair.ts <in> <out.mp4> --finalize [--abr 192k]` | Repair gate ticking; --finalize iterates until the encoded file scans clean |
| **BreathTame** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/BreathTame.ts <file> [--dry-run] [--json]` | Attenuate individual breath/mouth-click events in word gaps; word-confined, ducks never removes, proves bit-identity outside events |
| **LoudnessLock** | `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/Tools/LoudnessLock.ts <in> [--out <out.mp4>]` | Measure or lock delivery loudness to −14 LUFS / −1dBTP (YouTube standard); self re-measures, exit 0 only in tolerance |

## Gate Artifacts

Gate checks run only when someone actually reports ticking or clicking; routine per-export scans were retired 2026-07-15. On a report: `GateScan` the file to confirm (sample-domain steps, exit 1 on defects), then `GateRepair --finalize` to fix. Repair before leveling when possible, and scan the final encode, not the intermediate WAV. If a RAW recording scans dirty, a capture-chain gate is back on; surface it.

## API Keys Required

| Service | Env Var | Where to Get |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| Cleanvoice (for polish step, optional) | `CLEANVOICE_API_KEY` | cleanvoice.ai Dashboard Settings API Key |

## Gotchas

- **Cloud polish uploads audio to external service.** Confirm the user is okay with cloud processing for sensitive content.
- **Capture-chain noise gates cause the ticks.** Recorder filters and macOS Voice Isolation truncate audio to digital zero with no fade, and leveling amplifies each edge into an audible tick. The class is fixed at capture: remove any noise-gate filter from the recorder's mic chain. (2026-07-13: hundreds of gate edges in one recording reached published audio.)
- **AAC re-introduces steps near silence.** An intermediate WAV that scans clean says nothing about the encoded file, which is why GateScan runs on the final encode. (2026-07-13)
- **dB-domain cliff detectors false-positive on fade feet.** A legitimate cosine fade into digital zero has infinite dB slope at its foot, so any >NdB/2ms detector flags it forever. Verify repairs with sample-domain STEP detection (GateScan), never dB slopes. (2026-07-13)
- **One-sided iterative fades don't converge on stray boundary impulses.** A single sample sitting on a gate boundary survives repeated one-sided fades; fade-down-then-up "mutes" preserve a blip's edges and its leading step. The V-notch (cosine to zero at the boundary, both sides) and hard-zeroing inside gated silence are the converging fixes. (2026-07-13)
- **Meter-clean ≠ ear-clean.** Scanners find ticks; repairs can create audible holes the tick-scanner calls clean (the 2026-07-12 duck incident). Match the probe to the defect class a human hears, keep repairs minimal-touch, and give the principal before/after listen clips at swap time.

## Examples

- **"clean up the audio on this podcast file"** → Clean, full pipeline (transcribe → analyze → edit) → cleaned MP3 with filler words, stutters, and dead air removed.
- **"show me what edits you'd make to this recording"** → Clean with `--preview` → proposed edit list, audio untouched; the user reviews, then runs again to apply.
- **"aggressively clean this audio and polish it"** → Clean with `--aggressive --polish` → tighter filler thresholds, then the Cleanvoice pass for mouth sounds and normalization.

# BeCreative

Ask a model for "a creative idea" and you get the most probable one: the safe, already-seen answer. This skill pushes past that. Single-pass intents use Verbalized Sampling (generate several low-probability candidates, surface the strongest; see `ResearchFoundation.md`). SyntheticDataExpansion grows a small seed set into a diverse corpus. Ideas evolved over several rounds (a population of proposers, recombination with lineage, measured or cross-vendor fitness) are HillClimb's Ideate intent (`skills/HillClimb/Intents/Ideate.md`).

## Ideal State

- Each run surfaces several genuinely distinct candidates, compared against each other rather than by self-reported probability, and names the strongest for the brief.
- The candidates differ in kind (different assumptions, framings, formats or domains), never one idea in five outfits.
- When diversity is load-bearing, candidates are generated or judged across a second vendor, the lane chosen by whether the brief is taste-judged (Anthropic) or correctness-judged (OpenAI).
- SyntheticDataExpansion returns a corpus measurably more diverse than its seed set: a higher diversity index from `Tools/Diversity.ts index` than the seed.

# BiasCheck

Runs a three-layer bias audit on any source: a URL, a file path, or raw text. It reads the content plus any study it cites, then checks (1) biases inside the data, (2) conflicts of interest in the source organization, and (3) distortions the journalism added on top. The output separates what the data actually supports from what got editorialized.

## Ideal State

- Every audit reaches the primary source behind the input, or records that it could not as a finding.
- The three layers (data, source organization, journalism) stay separate, and every bias claim names a concrete tell from the artifact.
- The reader leaves with what the data actually supports, split from what was editorialized on top, so the original claim can be rewritten honestly.
- Findings are specific to this artifact. A funder's stake is a multiplier on the analysis, never an automatic disqualifier, and a category with no tell in the source is left out rather than forced.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Check** | "bias check", "analyze bias on", "check this study/source/article" | `Intents/Check.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `BiasTaxonomy.md` | naming a bias category: the full catalog with definitions, tells and worked examples |
| `EvalState.md` | checking the `biascheck-layers` eval score (machine-written by Assay, never hand-edited) |

## Data & Config

User customizations live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/BiasCheck/` (`configRoot` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When that directory exists, its `PREFERENCES.md` and reference files override the defaults here; when it is absent, the defaults stand.

## Gotchas

- **The biggest failure is never reaching the study.** Critiquing the headline without the underlying data misses whether the data was fine or junk; the Check intent's fetch order exists for this.

## Examples

**Example 1: Article citing a vendor study**
```
User: "bias check https://news.example.com/some-article-citing-a-vendor-survey"
→ Check intent
→ The cited vendor study is located and read alongside the article
→ Report covers the vendor conflict of interest, sample and question-design biases, and the headline-vs-source swap, then the supported-vs-editorialized split
```

**Example 2: Raw paste of a study abstract**
```
User: "bias check this abstract: [pastes 4 paragraphs from a paper]"
→ Check intent
→ Layers 1 and 2 only (funding disclosure, sample, methodology, conflict of interest); Layer 3 is skipped with a note because the input IS the primary source
→ The report says when the abstract is too thin to assess methodology (publication availability bias)
```

**Example 3: File path**
```
User: "bias check ~/Downloads/some-report.pdf"
→ Check intent
→ Upstream sources the report cites are fetched where possible
→ Three-layer report with specifics
```

# BitterLessonEngineering

Audits any AI instruction set for over-prompting: every rule goes through the Six Questions below and gets one classification from CUT to KEEP, with an estimate of the tokens saved. Two intents: Audit (full system) and QuickCheck (a single file or rule set). The core test for every rule: *"Would a smarter model make this unnecessary?"* If yes, it is scaffolding, not architecture, and a candidate to cut. Unnecessary rules compete for attention with the ones that matter, so a bloated setup produces worse output than a lean one.

## Ideal State

- Every audited rule is first sorted by kind under The First Sort below, and the report counts each kind. A preference is never cut, by judgment, score or ablation; a prescriptive step that is not a keep-class leaves as CUT or as REWRITE to the outcome it protects.
- Every audited rule carries one classification from the table below with a one-line reason, and no keep-class rule (safety gate, verified gotcha, tool contract, output-format contract) is ever marked CUT.
- No declarative content a model cannot derive (environment facts, domain invariants, API shapes, worked examples) is ever marked CUT; question 6 cuts imperative reasoning steps only.
- No rule is cut as default behavior unless it is still default on the current model and the failure it was added for is truly gone.
- Every report states its scope, the rule count and the verdict counts; a full audit also states estimated savings in lines and tokens.
- The audited files change only after the user approves the trimmed versions.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Audit** | "audit setup", "full audit", "check all rules" | `Intents/Audit.md` |
| **QuickCheck** | "quick check", "check this file", "check these rules" | `Intents/QuickCheck.md` |

## The First Sort

Whether a rule is BLE is decided by its kind, never by the length of the file it sits in (principal directive, 2026-10-25). Sort every rule into one kind before asking the Six Questions:

| Kind | What it says | Verdict |
|------|--------------|---------|
| **Preference** | What the principal wants: an outcome, a taste, a word's meaning, who is trusted, which tool is ours | **KEEP.** A smarter model still cannot know it. Questions 2, 3 and 5 may still MERGE, RESOLVE or SHARPEN it. |
| **Move guard** | What must exist before a move is allowed: evidence before a fix or a close, an approval before a deploy, an independent mind before a verdict, a re-check before building on uncertain direction, who rules a contradiction | **KEEP, rigid.** Its purpose is authority, accountability, independence, an external commitment or irreversibility, and a smarter model leaves each of those standing (author bias does not shrink with capability). System prompt § Rigid moves, free work. |
| **Prescriptive step** | How to do something: an order of actions, a method, reasoning choreography | **CUT**, or **REWRITE** as the outcome it protects, unless it is a move guard or safety gate |
| **Verified gotcha** | A non-obvious failure of a tool or the install | **KEEP** where it fires before the mistake; **MOVE to tool** once the tool can make the mistake impossible |
| **Tool contract** | An exact command, path, flag or API shape | **KEEP**, beside the outcome it serves |
| **Safety gate / output-format contract** | An approval or destructive-op guard; a required deliverable shape | **KEEP** |

A with/without ablation measures steps, never preferences: most tasks never exercise a given preference, so an ablation scores it useless and would delete what only the principal could say.

## The Six Questions

Ask each question of every rule, instruction, or preference found; a yes gives the verdict and action in its row.

| # | Question | Verdict | Action |
|---|----------|---------|--------|
| 1 | **Default behavior?** Does Claude already do this without being told? | **CUT** | The model already does this. |
| 2 | **Contradiction?** Does it conflict with another rule in the same or a different file? | **RESOLVE** | Pick one, cut the other. |
| 3 | **Redundancy?** Is it already covered by a different rule or file? | **MERGE** | One location, one statement. |
| 4 | **One-off fix?** Was it added to fix one specific bad output rather than improve outputs generally? | **EVALUATE** | Still relevant, or already learned? |
| 5 | **Vague?** Would Claude interpret it differently every time (e.g., "be more natural", numeric personality scales)? | **SHARPEN** | Add specific DO/DON'T examples, or cut. |
| 6 | **HOW instead of WHAT?** Is it **procedural over-prompting**: does it dictate execution methodology or reasoning choreography ("first analyze X, then consider Y, then decide Z") instead of articulating the ideal state (WHAT done looks like) plus the tools? | **CUT** | Scaffolding, unless it is a keep-class or declarative content. |

Two verdicts sit outside the questions. Content that is loaded but rarely actionable gets **MOVE to on-demand**: load it via the CLAUDE.md routing table when needed. A rule that is specific, actionable and non-default gets **KEEP**, which is what good instructions look like.

Declarative content is **KEEP**, never scaffolding: environment facts, domain invariants, API shapes and worked examples a model cannot derive. They state what is true, not how to reason, so question 6 does not reach them. Four keep-classes are legitimate HOW, never cut them: **safety-gate** (confirmation/destructive-op guard/approval), **verified-gotcha** (a documented non-obvious failure), **tool-contract** (exact CLI/API/path recipe), **output-format-contract** (required deliverable shape). Deterministic tools (`*.ts`) are exempt. A rule that survives "would a smarter model make this unnecessary?" is either a keep-class or genuine architecture. Infrastructure that makes output checkable (verification harnesses, ISC, data pipelines, routing rules) is architecture; machinery wrapped around the model's reasoning (CoT orchestrators, format parsers, retry cascades, process descriptions that aren't followed) is scaffolding. Full doctrine: `LIFEOS/RULES/Philosophy.md` § Ideal-State Prompting.

## Gotchas

- Process doctrine (the Algorithm, a release flow, an SOP) is mostly move guards, and they read like steps. On 2026-10-25 a first pass over the Algorithm marked "reproduce before fixing", "a fresh mind after two failed fixes" and "two re-calls, then the principal rules" as prescriptive steps to cut; all three are guards. Ask what the step protects before calling it method.
- File length is not the finding. When OPERATIONAL_PREFERENCES.md was sorted on 2026-10-25, about 8 of its 359 rule lines were prescriptive steps; the rest were preferences, gotchas and tool contracts. An audit that reported "91 dated directives" as drift was wrong until it sorted them.
- Cutting domain content as choreography costs quality: in the 2026-10-10 skill-quality A/B, FirstPrinciples lost −0.122 after its domain content was cut as methodology and won +0.089 once it was restored.
- Startup context includes CLAUDE.md `@`-imports and the `dynamicContext` settings key (the full list of force-loaded sources is `Intents/Audit.md` § Inputs) — `loadAtStartup` was retired at v5.0's move to `@`-imports, and `postCompactRestore` no longer ships in any settings file. A reference to either in an instruction file is dead weight to flag, not a sync obligation. <!-- public PR #2008, @jbmml -->
- Deterministic drift detection exists: `bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/SkillDriftLint.ts --dir skills/ [--strict] [--top N]` (ported from @rpriven, public issue #1523). It is an advisory-only V1/V2 pattern scan: use it to find candidates mechanically, then judge each against the four keep-classes with this skill's questions. Drift grows back after every cut; the linter is the continuous check, this skill is the judgment.

## Examples

**Example 1: Full system audit**
```
User: "Run BLE on my setup"
→ Audit intent
→ A categorized report over every force-loaded file with estimated token savings, trimmed versions offered for approval
```

**Example 2: Check a single file**
```
User: "Quick check this CLAUDE.md"
→ QuickCheck intent
→ A concise keep/cut/sharpen verdict for every rule in the file
```

**Example 3: Post-cleanup validation**
```
User: "I trimmed my rules, check if anything's still redundant"
→ Audit intent
→ Any surviving dead weight flagged against current Claude defaults
```

# Brand

# BrightData

Fetches a single URL (FourTierScrape) or crawls a whole site (Crawl), moving through four tiers only as far as each page needs, always within the target site's terms and robots.txt. A site that refuses automated access is reported, not worked around. Output is always markdown. A Cloudflare `Accept: text/markdown` pre-check runs before Tier 1 (recipe in FourTierScrape.md).

## Ideal State

- Every page comes back as clean markdown that matches its URL, labeled with the tier that actually retrieved it.
- Cost tracks need: free tiers are tried first, and paid Bright Data calls (Tier 4, whether for one URL or for the pages of a Light Crawl that need it, and Full Crawl) happen only when cheaper ones fail or the user confirms.
- A crawl returns a site map, the page contents and its stats, with failed pages named rather than silently missing.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| FourTierScrape | "scrape/fetch/pull/get/retrieve [URL]", "fetch this page as markdown", "this page needs rendering", "use Bright Data to fetch" | `Intents/FourTierScrape.md` |
| Crawl | "crawl this site", "spider this domain", "map this website", "get all pages from", "scrape the whole site", "crawl all pages under /docs" | `Intents/Crawl.md` |

### References

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: the free tiers, the paid Bright Data pieces (MCP server, API key, crawl dataset id), and a proof |

## The four tiers (tool contract)

| Tier | Tool | Wins on | Cost / latency |
|------|------|---------|----------------|
| 1 | plain `curl -sL`, raw HTML converted to markdown locally | public content | free · ~1-3s |
| 2 | curl + declared user agent and Accept headers | servers that need content negotiation | free · ~3-7s |
| 3 | Interceptor (real Chrome) | JavaScript-rendered / SPA pages | free · ~10-20s |
| 4 | Bright Data MCP `mcp__Brightdata__scrape_as_markdown` | managed rendering, region-specific fetches | Bright Data credits · ~5-15s |

Every tier returns the page itself. WebFetch is never a tier: it hands back a small model's summary of the page, not the page.

Skip-ahead: explicit "use Bright Data" → Tier 4; "use browser" → Tier 3; a domain that already failed Tier 1 for a non-refusal reason (empty body, timeout) → start at Tier 2. A CAPTCHA, block page or login wall at any tier ends the retrieval with a report. The exact curl header block, Cloudflare pre-check, and Interceptor commands live in `Intents/FourTierScrape.md`.

## Data & Config

User customizations live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/BrightData/` (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there; they override default behavior. If it does not exist, proceed with skill defaults. First-time setup (accounts, keys, config, a proof it works) is in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

The paid paths need pieces this skill does not install. Tier 4 needs the Bright Data MCP server, which supplies `mcp__Brightdata__scrape_as_markdown` and `scrape_batch`. Full Crawl needs `BRIGHT_DATA_API_KEY` and `BRIGHT_DATA_CRAWL_DATASET_ID` (the Crawl API dataset id from the Bright Data dashboard) in the environment. Before the first paid call, confirm the MCP tools are present in the session and that `bun LIFEOS/TOOLS/Secrets.ts has BRIGHT_DATA_API_KEY BRIGHT_DATA_CRAWL_DATASET_ID` prints `yes` for each key the call needs. When a piece is missing, stop at the last free tier and tell the user which piece is not configured; never report a Tier 4 or Full Crawl result that did not run.

## Gotchas

- **Bright Data proxy has usage costs.** Don't use Tier 4 for sites accessible via Tier 1-3.
- **Tier 4 is slower than the free tiers.** Allow extra time for its responses.
- **Credentials belong in `~/.claude/.env`** — BRIGHT_DATA_API_KEY (the name `Intents/Crawl.md` commands read). Check as Data & Config says instead of assuming the paid tiers work.

## Examples

- "Fetch example.com/pricing as markdown" → FourTierScrape. The pre-check returns HTML, Tier 1 returns an empty body, and Tier 2's declared headers get the page, delivered as markdown labeled Tier 2. If Tier 1 had returned a block page instead, the reply would report the block and stop.
- "Crawl the docs under docs.example.com/api/" → Crawl, a Light Crawl scoped to `/api/`, depth 3, at the default limit of 20 pages, which needs no confirmation (more than 20 does). Each page climbs the tiers on its own, and any page that needed Tier 4 is named in the stats with its cost.
- "Use Bright Data to fetch this region-specific listing" → FourTierScrape, skipping to Tier 4. If the MCP server is not registered, the reply says so and offers the best free-tier result.

# Broadcast Skill

**Contents:** Ideal State · Intent Routing · Platforms · Data & Config · Gotchas · Examples

Posts to X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Bluesky and Instagram from one command, and also publishes X Articles, podcast episodes to Omny Studio and newsletter share posts. It checks each platform's character and media limits before sending, previews with `--dry-run`, and reports per-platform status. Auth is per platform (table under Platforms; first-time setup in `Setup.md`, day-two auth in `Intents/Auth.md`). X posting runs through the public `X` skill's tools and its OAuth 2.0 token store. This skill posts; it does not write the copy, which comes from a copywriting skill or the principal first.

## Ideal State

- A broadcast reaches every platform the principal named, and "all channels", "everywhere", "all three" or "all four" means all four; a platform that fails or is skipped is reported with its reason while the rest still post.
- Each platform gets text that fits its own limit and format before anything is sent: X text is weighed and never sliced, and styled LinkedIn text goes in a run of its own.
- When the principal hands over written prose, their words go out verbatim with only platform markup added; drafting new copy belongs to a copywriting skill.
- A cross-post of the principal's latest X post ("put my latest tweet on LinkedIn and Insta") carries that post's exact text and media, read back from X with `X/Tools/read.ts`, with t.co links expanded to their real URLs and nothing added beyond LinkedIn styling.
- Nothing public goes out unpreviewed: a `--dry-run` comes first, irreversible publishes (an X Article, a live podcast episode) wait for confirmation, and success is reported from what the platform returned (post links, X `expanded_url` matching the canonical URL, a verified Omny publish).

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **X** | "post to X", "tweet", "post to Twitter" | `Intents/X.md` |
| **Article** | "post an article to X", "publish as an X article", "long-form on X", "intro post plus article link" | `Intents/Article.md` |
| **LinkedIn** | "post to LinkedIn", "LinkedIn post" | `Intents/LinkedIn.md` |
| **Bluesky** | "post to Bluesky", "Bluesky post" | `Intents/Bluesky.md` |
| **Instagram** | "post to Instagram", "Instagram post", "reel", "carousel" | `Intents/Instagram.md` |
| **Podcast** | "post as podcast", "publish podcast episode", "put this on the podcast", "Omny" | `Intents/Podcast.md` |
| **ShareNewsletter** | "share the newsletter", "newsletter share post", "post the newsletter to LinkedIn", "share this week's edition", "edition share card", "sponsor thank-you in the share" | `Intents/ShareNewsletter.md` |
| **Post** | "broadcast", "post to all", "cross-post" | `Intents/Post.md` |
| **Status** | "check status", "platform status" | `Intents/Status.md` |
| **Auth** | "configure", "auth", "setup platform" | `Intents/Auth.md` |
| **SecurityValidation** | "validate content", "check post" | `Intents/SecurityValidation.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: the Config.md fields, each platform's account and secrets, the scheduled token renewal, and the proof it works |
| `Tools/` | running a platform tool directly; `Tools/LinkedInAuth.help.md` is the full `LinkedInAuth.ts` contract (the tool itself prints a one-line usage) |

## Platforms

| Platform | Auth | Images | Videos | Media limits | Text limit |
|----------|------|--------|--------|--------------|------------|
| Twitter/X | OAuth 2.0 user context (the X skill's token store); OAuth 1.0a keys for text only | Up to 4 | 1 per post | Images: 5MB, Videos: 512MB | 280 weighted characters (URLs = 23) |
| LinkedIn | OAuth 2.0 access token | Up to 20 (multiImage) | 1 per post | Images: 8MB, Videos: 500MB | 3,000 |
| Bluesky | App password | Up to 4 | 1 per post | Images: 1MB, Videos: 50MB | 300 |
| Instagram | Instagram Login (60-day token) | Up to 10 (carousel) | 1 (Reel) | Images: 8MB JPEG, Videos: 300MB | 2,200 |
| Podcast (Omny Studio) | OMNYSTUDIO_API_KEY | | | | |
| X Articles (long-form) | Same X OAuth 2.0 store | | | | |

**Supported formats:**
- Images: JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP (Instagram auto-converts to JPEG)
- Videos: MP4, MOV, AVI, WebM

`--media` takes local file paths only; a remote URL fails with "Media file not found". **Instagram is media-required** (no text-only posts) and JPEG-only for images; its R2 staging contract is in `Intents/Instagram.md`.

Post logs append to `LIFEOS/MEMORY/STATE/Broadcast-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` under your LifeOS directory (`~/.claude/LIFEOS` by default; `LIFEOS_BROADCAST_LOG_DIR` overrides it), outside the skill dir. The CLI entry points are `bun ${LIFEOS_SKILL_DIR}/src/index.ts` and its alias `Tools/Broadcast.ts`; each intent carries its own commands.

## Data & Config

The skill body carries no handles, program IDs or newsletter identity. Account-bound values live outside
the skill tree (release-excluded) in `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Broadcast/Config.md`: the Omny
program, playlist ids and episode settings, which `Tools/OmnyPublish.ts` reads at runtime through
`src/skill-config.ts`; the newsletter name, URL, edition label, the optional share features (sponsor thank-yous, the edition
share card and its brand file, the card file prefix, the writing audit) and an optional house-rules overlay,
which the ShareNewsletter intent reads; the optional posting preferences `house_style` and `video_followup` (both off by default), which `post`, `edit` and the platform intents read; and the account handles for reference. Every key, with a made-up example, is in `Setup.md`. X's token store is configured
in the X skill's own Config.md (`skills/X/Setup.md`). Per-platform API keys are env-var names whose values
live in `~/.claude/.env`; LinkedIn, Bluesky and Instagram sessions live in `~/.broadcast/credentials.json`.

## Gotchas

- **"All channels" includes Instagram, which needs media.** A post with no media still goes to the three text platforms and reports Instagram as skipped, so ship an image whenever one exists.
- **LinkedIn styling is converted from markdown, and required only under the house style.** `**bold**`, `# Header` and the rest become LinkedIn's styled text (the table in `Intents/LinkedIn.md`). With `house_style = true` in Config.md, every LinkedIn post (cross-posts, newsletter shares, edits) carries a `**bold**` hook line or `# Header` lines, the author's words stay verbatim with only the markup added, and `post` and `edit` refuse LinkedIn content with no bold span or header line (exit 1, dry-run included); `--linkedin-plain` is the named exception. With the key absent or `false` (the default), plain text posts as written. Either way, because `**` would show raw on X and Bluesky, LinkedIn gets its own run with its own styled file whenever styled text is shared with another platform.
- **X text is weighted, never raw-truncated.** Every HTTP(S) URL counts as 23 characters, while Unicode uses X's code-point/emoji weighting. `X/Tools/TwitterText.ts` is the shared validator used by Broadcast and `X/Tools/post.ts`. Preserve the caller's exact text and full canonical URLs; if weighted length exceeds 280, fail closed instead of slicing or adding an ellipsis. After publishing, read the returned tweet with `X/Tools/read.ts` and confirm each `expanded_url` equals the intended canonical URL before reporting success.
- **Every video passes the PII gate before upload** (`LIFEOS/TOOLS/VideoPiiGate.ts`, run by `post` and `article`): findings stop the post until you add `--pii-reviewed`; `--skip-pii` bypasses the scan loudly and is for when the scanner is down only.
- **The send gate proofs the exact bytes each platform receives.** `post` runs SendGate's code-tier proof (`LIFEOS/TOOLS/lib/SendGate.ts`) on each platform's wire text and media immediately before the network call; a fail closes that platform and nothing is transmitted. Two LinkedIn exceptions: a LinkedIn video is held to LinkedIn's own spec and the video PII gate, not to the proof's file checks, and it uploads from its original path; and a link card's title, description and image are fetched from the linked page at send time, so the gate never sees them (on a URL-only post the commentary is that fetched title, and the gate proofs the URL).
- **LinkedIn's `commentary` field is "little text format" — unescaped `( ) [ ] { } < > @ # * _ ~ |` silently swallow content.** The API returns 201 and the post publishes truncated at the first reserved char, so a hook like "(No. 42) is out" is cut mid-line. `escapeLittleText()` in `src/format/linkedin-formatter.ts` escapes these outside URLs, well-formed mentions, and letter-led `#Word` hashtags (`#42` still escapes), and `assertLittleText()` runs on the exact wire string before POST and throws on any unescaped reserved char, so this class now fails loud instead of shipping truncated. Truncation never cuts inside a mention. Dry-run shows the styled text without the escaping backslashes, cut where the escaped wire form is cut, with the link-card URL on its own line.
- **Auth tokens expire.** If posting fails, re-check OAuth tokens for each platform before debugging the content.
- **ALL X posting — text and media — runs on the X skill's OAuth 2.0 token store.** The twitter adapter hands every post to `X/Tools/post.ts`, which uses OAuth 2.0 user context (`tweet.write` + `media.write` + `offline.access`). Where the grant lives and who refreshes it is the X skill's Config.md, never this skill's. With no store configured, `post.ts` falls back to the OAuth 1.0a env keys for text only; X can revoke those keys without notice and they have no media path, so a split path would post text while video silently fails. A twitter 401 on text means the grant lost `tweet.write`; a **403 on media means the grant is missing `media.write`** — either way, re-auth once via `X/Tools/bookmarks.ts authorize`.
- **`status`'s twitter row verifies the path posting will use.** It checks the X skill's token store first (`hasOAuth2Store()`) and calls `/users/me` through it; only with no store does it verify the OAuth 1.0a keys. Keys that merely sit in `.env` never count as connected, because revoked keys look exactly like live ones until a call fails.

## Examples

```
User: "put my latest tweet on linkedin and insta"
→ Post intent
→ The X post's exact text, links expanded, is live on LinkedIn (bold hook added) and on Instagram with its image, both links reported
```

```
User: "Post to LinkedIn only: 'Finally moved the whole build to the new toolchain.' with link https://example.com/blog/toolchain"
→ LinkedIn intent
→ The post is live with the words verbatim and the article's link-preview card, and the post link is reported
```

```
User: "post my video ./my-export.mp4 to Instagram"  (the user's own local file; given only a link, the run asks for the local file and never downloads it)
→ Instagram intent
→ The file passes the PII gate and is live as a Reel; the Reel link is reported
```
