# RichFormat

**Contents:** Ideal State · Anti-criteria · Intent Routing · What it draws · The LifeOS rule · Tool contracts · Data & Config · Gotchas · Examples

A function-hooks plugin that makes assistant replies faster to read in the terminal. Claude Code loads it from this folder in every interactive session. It hooks two events and nothing else:

- `prompt.compose` adds one section to the system prompt that teaches the drawable conventions, in interactive terminal sessions only (Anti-criteria).
- `classic.MessageDisplay` receives each batch of finished lines while an answer streams and returns the text the terminal shows in their place, with ANSI colour. That text is the answer's first and only copy. A drawable fence is held until it closes, then drawn whole (`hooks/stream.ts`).

## Ideal State

- Every construct in What it draws that parses is drawn, never left as plain markdown: a `flow` fence as boxed nodes, a `diff` fence as numbered red and green lines, a fully marked VERIFY run as green and red marks, and a label line in its colour (the engine and pure-logic suites hold each).
- The stored message never changes. The model, the transcript file and ctrl+o all see plain markdown.
- On any doubt the lines show as written: a fence that does not parse, a fence still open at the message's last flush, a thrown error, or the option switched off.
- Every answer prints exactly once, at any length, under the full statusline.

## Anti-criteria

- The mod never hooks any event besides `prompt.compose` and `classic.MessageDisplay`; no `ui.render` hook on AssistantMessage comes back, even one that passes the answer straight through.
- A finished answer is never repainted; this mod shapes first draws only.
- The prompt section is never added outside an interactive terminal session, so iMessage bridges, `-p` runs, teammates and SDK sessions never learn a convention they cannot draw.
- A list is never split between two renderers: a 💡 line inside a list or table, a ✓ bullet outside VERIFY, a VERIFY run with any unmarked or nested bullet, and anything inside another code fence stay plain.
- A double-printed answer is never fixed by turning the statusline off.

## Intent Routing

No intents: the plugin runs on its own. Reference files:

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup, or filling in the optional USER `Config.md` and `PREFERENCES.md` |

## What it draws

| Written in the reply | Drawn as |
|---|---|
| A fenced `flow` block, one `a -> b -> c` chain per line | Rows of boxed nodes joined by `▶`, wrapped to the terminal width |
| A fenced `bar` block of `label: value` lines | A horizontal bar chart, cyan bars, values as written (`hooks/charts.ts`) |
| A fenced `spark` block, one series of numbers per line | A one-line trend with its min, max and last |
| A fenced `tree` block holding an indented outline | A hierarchy drawn with `├─`, `│` and `└─` |
| A fenced `timeline` block of `when: what` lines | Events on a vertical rail with a `●` per event |
| A fenced `diff` block holding one valid unified-diff hunk | Old and new line numbers, removals red, additions green |
| `🔧 CHANGE:`, `✅ VERIFY:`, `❓ OPEN:` label lines | Bold blue, green and yellow labels |
| A standalone line starting with 💡 or ⚠️ | A cyan or amber bar before the line |
| A VERIFY run whose bullets all start `- ✓` or `- ✗` | Green and red marks |
| A markdown table (header, delimiter row, body), held until it ends | A rounded box grid: frame grey, header bold soft blue, numeric columns right-aligned, ✓ ✗ ⚠ cells toned, cell markdown escaped (`hooks/table.ts`) |
| `#`/`##` and `###` headings, a lone `**Mini header**`, a 🎯 line | Bold accent blue, bold soft blue, bold soft blue, bold; markers removed (`hooks/enrich.ts`) |
| `- ` items and `1. ` items | An accent `•` (nested: grey `◦`) and an accent number (yellow in OPEN), wrapped with a hanging indent |
| `---` (or `* * *`), `> quote` | A grey `─` rule the content width; a grey `▎` bar |
| A fenced `workflow` block holding one line, `wf_<id> <plain summary>` | That run's brief card from the bridge (below); the stored text stays the one summary line (`hooks/workflow.ts`) |
| A `🗣️ Name:` closer line outside a code fence | The LifeOS rule on its own line just above it: `━━ ◆ LifeOS ━━━ <isa slug> <done>/<total> ━━`, name bold #3B82F6, rule dim, state cyan |

A chart block with any line that does not parse, more than 40 lines, or too little width to draw stays plain code.

The workflow card comes from `HookBridge.ts workflow-card <session id> <run id> <columns>`, run as an argv array with a 3 s timeout, only for the flush that closes the fence: at most 3 cards per flush and 12 lines per card, escape sequences other than colour stripped. An id that is not `wf_…`, a failed bridge or any other answer leaves the fence as written. The prompt section teaches the fence (`WORKFLOW_FENCE_TEXT` in `hooks/workflow.ts`).

## The LifeOS rule

- It is drawn only by this mod, only on the terminal, on its own line just above a `🗣️ Name:` closer, with a blank line each side. It is the terminal width (read once per 5 s with `stty -f /dev/tty size`, 80 when that fails) minus the 2-cell reply gutter.
- The state (slug and progress) comes from `HookBridge.ts band-state <session id>`, run as an argv array with a 3 s timeout, only for the flush that holds the closer. No session or a failed bridge draws the bare rule with no state.
- Rule and closer logic live in `hooks/banner.ts`, the streamed drawing in `hooks/stream.ts`; `hooks/register.tsx` only wires them.

## Tool contracts

- Validate: `claude plugin validate --json skills/RichFormat`
- Engine tests (only `*.test.tsx` here, run in the hooks sandbox): `cd skills/RichFormat && claude plugin test .`
- Pure-logic suites (`*.spec.ts`, run under bun): `cd skills/RichFormat && bun test ./tests/<name>.spec.ts`
- Typecheck: `cd skills/RichFormat && bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`
- Off switch: the plugin's `enabled` option (`userConfig`, default on). Off draws every reply exactly as the engine does and adds no prompt section.
- Terminal font: the drawn markers are Nerd Font symbols (`hooks/glyph-core.ts`), so the terminal needs a Nerd Font; see `Setup.md` § Terminal font.

## Data & Config

Install-specific values live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/RichFormat/` (`configRoot` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`): `Config.md` holds `marketplace` (the plugin marketplace the mod loads from), and `PREFERENCES.md` holds the principal's display preferences. When the directory is absent, the defaults here stand: the mod draws the same way and only the reload advice is generic. `Setup.md` documents each key.

## Gotchas

- **`claude plugin test` loads every `*.test.ts` and `*.test.tsx` under the folder inside the hooks sandbox, which refuses any import except relative files and `claude-code`.** A `bun:test` suite named `*.test.ts` makes the whole run exit 1. The bun suites are `*.spec.ts` for that reason (2026-10-04).
- **The hooks loader refuses a module that stores, passes or returns `$` itself.** It must be spelled `$.noun.event(...)` at the call site. A holder (`host.current = $`) stopped the whole mod loading, so every reply fell back to the engine. Hand closures that spell `$.…` inside them instead (`BridgeCalls` in `hooks/register.tsx`). Lanes cannot run `claude plugin test`, so run it in the main session before landing anything that touches `register.tsx` (2026-10-04).
- **Never repaint a finished answer.** Re-rendering an answer that had scrolled above the viewport smeared it, character-interleaved (2026-09-16). This mod shapes first draws only; `tests/hooked-events.check.ts` and the no-`invalidate` check hold that.
- **Never hook `ui.render` on AssistantMessage again: any hook that can see a finished answer makes a tall turn print twice, even one that passes it straight through (2026-10-09).** The engine draws an answer itself while it streams and asks the hooks only once it settles, so whatever a hook returns is a second copy under the statusline: the engine repaints the live turn, and the main screen keeps the scrolled-off copy. A tree cell-identical to the engine's drawing still doubled most rows, and so did a synchronous hook (2026-10-07). The `SHORT_ANSWER` matcher did not save it: under a tall statusline the live area overflows even for short answers, and a short answer printed twice on 2026-10-09. `classic.MessageDisplay` is the only door: it draws the first copy. `tests/hooked-events.check.ts` fails if `ui.render` comes back. Installs run with the statusline on (the principal's standing preference is in the USER `PREFERENCES.md`, § Data & Config), so never fix this by turning it off. Probe: a background kitty tab answering a 60-row prompt, then `kitty @ get-text --extent all` counts repeated rows.
- **A diff the engine's parser refuses is drawn as grey plain code, which looks worse than plain Markdown.** `hooks/diff.ts` accepts only bodies stricter than the engine's jsdiff `parsePatch`. `tests/diff.spec.ts` checks parity against jsdiff from the local bun cache and fails, rather than skips, when it cannot load it (2026-10-04).
- **Box and arrow glyphs are one cell; emoji and ⚠️ with variation selector 16 are two.** `displayWidth` in `hooks/flow.ts` measures cells, and diagrams keep a two-cell margin. A one-cell overflow hard-wraps a row and breaks the box.
- **When the mods load from a local folder marketplace, a saved edit reaches no open session until `/reload-plugins` there**, and a module that fails to load leaves the engine drawing every reply itself. The install's marketplace name is the `marketplace` key in the USER `Config.md` (§ Data & Config); LifeOSHooks SKILL.md has the wiring (§ Gotchas, the local-marketplace entry) and the 2026-10-11 miss (§ Anti-criteria).

## Examples

**Example 1: A flow diagram shows as plain code**
```
User: "flow diagram not drawn"
→ Check the fence parses: one `a -> b -> c` chain per line, at most 40 lines, and enough terminal width to draw it
→ Check the mod is loaded: from a local folder marketplace, edits wait for /reload-plugins, and a broken module draws every reply as the engine does
→ claude plugin validate --json skills/RichFormat and the engine tests name the failure
```

**Example 2: An answer printed twice**
```
User: "the answer printed twice under the statusline"
→ bun ./tests/hooked-events.check.ts in skills/RichFormat: any hook besides prompt.compose and classic.MessageDisplay is the cause
→ Remove that hook; the statusline stays on
→ Probe with the 60-row kitty tab from Gotchas and count repeated rows
```

**Example 3: A workflow card did not draw**
```
User: "the workflow card shows as a code block"
→ The fence must hold exactly one line led by the wf_ id the Workflow tool returned
→ Run HookBridge.ts workflow-card <session id> <run id> 100 and check it prints {lines: [...]} within 3 s
```

# RootCauseAnalysis Skill

RootCauseAnalysis investigates incidents and recurring failures with causal methods (Five Whys, Fishbone, blameless Postmortem, Fault Tree, Kepner-Tregoe) and traces them to systemic root causes rather than to a person to blame. Apollo/RealityCharting and FMEA are supporting methods documented in `Foundation.md` and `MethodSelection.md`, not separate intents.

## Ideal State

- The method fits the failure class, as the situation table under Intent Routing maps it, and a non-trivial incident is written as a Postmortem with the other methods as its investigation tools.
- Every diagnosis is evidence-backed and blameless, with 3+ actionable systemic contributing factors rather than a single blame target. It ends at causes that are both systemic and within authority to change, never at a person to blame, and each corrective action prevents a class of recurrence rather than the latest trigger.
- Every conclusion that rests on a fact the request supplied cites that fact, checked at its source, and a caller's hypothesis is never taken as fact.
- Decisions are judged using the information available at the time.
- What the evidence cannot support is disclosed as a gap or a hypothesis, never filled with invented causes, probabilities or comparisons, and never padded with invented factors to meet the 3+ target.
- The analysis delivered is finished; no sub-work is still running when it is handed over.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **FiveWhys** | "5 whys", "five whys", quick causal chain, ask why until root | `Intents/FiveWhys.md` |
| **Fishbone** | "fishbone", "ishikawa", categorized cause map, 6 M's / 4 P's / 8 M's | `Intents/Fishbone.md` |
| **Postmortem** | "postmortem", "incident review", "blameless postmortem", production incident | `Intents/Postmortem.md` |
| **FaultTree** | "fault tree", "fta", top-down deductive, safety-critical, AND/OR logic | `Intents/FaultTree.md` |
| **KepnerTregoe** | "kepner tregoe", "is/is-not", "what changed", distinction analysis, subtle defects | `Intents/KepnerTregoe.md` |

| Situation | Preferred intent |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Single-thread incident, one clear failure point | **FiveWhys** |
| Multiple suspected categories (people, process, tools) | **Fishbone** |
| Production outage or security incident, needs formal review | **Postmortem** |
| Complex multi-path failure, safety-critical, need Boolean logic | **FaultTree** |
| Subtle defect, hard to reproduce, "why here and not there?" | **KepnerTregoe** |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `MethodSelection.md` | choosing, combining or switching methods: decision flow, method comparison, domain map, speed-versus-thoroughness |
| `Foundation.md` | evidence crosses service boundaries, or the work uses Apollo evidence graphs or FMEA prioritization |

Standalone; no required skill dependency. Use SystemsThinking (Iceberg, FindArchetype) for recurring structural causes, FirstPrinciples to decompose a contributing factor, RedTeam to stress-test remediations, and Science for investigation hypotheses.

## Data & Config

User customizations live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/RootCauseAnalysis/` (`configRoot` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When that directory exists, its `PREFERENCES.md`, configurations and resources apply and override the defaults here; when it is absent, the defaults stand.

## Gotchas

- Start from the facts and paths the request supplies and read those paths; do not search for them again. Any search names the paths it covers, never the whole home tree or ~/Projects. This scopes where to look, never what may be investigated.

## Examples

**Example 1: Production outage**
```
User: "Payments threw 500s for ten minutes after last night's deploy. Write the postmortem."
→ Postmortem intent, with FiveWhys or Fishbone on each contributing thread
→ A blameless record with a UTC timeline, defensive-layer map and strength-rated owned actions
```

**Example 2: Works here, not there**
```
User: "The export job fails only on the EU cluster and only on Mondays. Why?"
→ KepnerTregoe intent
→ An IS/IS-NOT matrix, the change that explains every IS without predicting the IS-NOTs, and a test to confirm it
```

**Example 3: Quick causal chain**
```
User: "5 whys on why the nightly backup keeps missing its window"
→ FiveWhys intent
→ An evidenced chain to systemic causes, read forward with no gaps, and owned corrective actions
```

# Science

Applies the scientific method to understanding a problem: a checkable goal fixed before evidence, competing falsifiable hypotheses, the evidence that tells them apart, and a decision on what to do next. DefineGoal frames the problem, QuickDiagnosis handles timeboxed debugging, and StructuredInvestigation runs the whole loop at working grade or research grade. Improving a target by measured experiment (hypotheses for a change, experiment design, reading results, iterating) is HillClimb's job, and `skills/HillClimb/References/Experiments.md` describes a well-framed experiment; a climb that stalls on a wrong frame comes back here. Use IterativeDepth for multi-lens exploration.

## Ideal State

- Every investigation ties a goal locked before evidence collection to competing falsifiable hypotheses, and every verdict traces to evidence against those precommitted criteria.
- Rigor matches the stakes: a quick diagnosis stays timeboxed, a complex problem leaves an auditable record, and a research-grade question gets pre-registration and independent review.
- Goal achievement and hypothesis support are judged separately, null and inconclusive results stay visible, and every investigation ends in an explicit next action or stopping decision.
- A question that turns into "make this measured number better" leaves Science for HillClimb with its goal and hypotheses attached.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **DefineGoal** | "define the goal", "what are we trying to achieve" | `Intents/DefineGoal.md` |
| **QuickDiagnosis** | Quick debugging (15-min rule); not for an obvious five-minute fix or creative/generative work, which need no ceremony | `Intents/QuickDiagnosis.md` |
| **StructuredInvestigation** | "investigate", complex or research-grade investigation | `Intents/StructuredInvestigation.md` |

Experiment requests ("what might work", "how do we test", "iterate", "analyze the results", "optimize") on a target with a measurement go to HillClimb (`skills/HillClimb/SKILL.md`).

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Methodology.md` | running or measuring an investigation: execution invariants and tool routing |
| `Protocol.md` | handing work to a specialist skill, sizing formality by scale, or receiving a stalled climb; also the contract a skill follows when its body says it implements the Science protocol |
| `Templates.md` | a record's status values or its compact form |
| `Examples.md` | interpreting improvement when the goal is still unmet, or an aggregate score against failed criteria |

## Data & Config

User customizations live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Science/` (`configRoot` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When that directory exists, its PREFERENCES.md, configurations and resources override the defaults here; when it is absent, the defaults stand.

## Gotchas

_No gotchas documented yet. Add failures here as they're discovered._

## Examples

- "Why is this test flaky?" → QuickDiagnosis: a one-sentence GOAL, H1-H3 with falsifiers, the cheapest discriminating test first.

- "What might work to cut churn?" → HillClimb: churn is a measured product number, so it is a metric climb with its hypotheses, experiments and keeps in the climb ledger.

- A weeks-long decision needing methodology review and statistical rigor → StructuredInvestigation at research grade: pre-registered goal, five or more hypotheses, independent review recorded.

# SecurityMarketData

Query Return on Security's Signal data through its live MCP interface, with evidence, freshness, and analytical boundaries intact.

## Ideal State

- Every answer comes from live Signal records reached through an authenticated `signal-mcp` (or the REST fallback when `ROS_API_KEY` exists), never from scraping, memory or an invented taxonomy.
- A reader can tell observed records from analytical outputs (forecasts, scores, suggestions) and sees the provider's freshness and quota as returned.

| Intent | Trigger | File |

| **QueryMarket** | Any supported market, company, investor, funding, M&A, or lifecycle query | `Intents/QueryMarket.md` |

Before executing, check `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/SecurityMarketData/`. If present, load enabled preferences and configuration; otherwise use these defaults. (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`)

First-time setup (the MCP server, the account, the sign-in) is in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

## Gotchas

# SecurityUpdates

Aggregates security news from six authoritative sources (§ Sources) into a ranked, deduplicated digest of up to 32 items across three categories: Security News, Security Research, and Security Ideas. A per-item record of what each run showed, kept in last-check.json by `Tools/Digest.ts`, avoids re-surfacing seen items, so a weekly run shows only what is new instead of the overlapping stories six sites publish on their own cadences.

## Ideal State

- A run returns at most 32 items, deduplicated across sources, ranked within News, Research and Ideas, each attributed to its source, and none fabricated.
- Nothing surfaced on an earlier run surfaces again, dated or not: every shown item's key is recorded in `MEMORY/STATE/SecurityUpdates-last-check.json` after each successful run, and the next run's candidates are filtered against it by `Tools/Digest.ts` (`Intents/Update.md` § Tool contract).
- Items come only from the configured sources: the six defaults in `sources.json`, swapped or extended through PREFERENCES.md.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Update** | "security updates", "sec updates", "/secupdates", "what's new in security" | `Intents/Update.md` |

**Default:** Run the Update intent.

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: the smallest working PREFERENCES.md, accounts (none) and the proof command |
| `Tools/Digest.help.md` | the state filter, recorder and digest check the Update intent runs |

## Data & Config

User customizations, read before each run:
`<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/SecurityUpdates/PREFERENCES.md`
configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`.

If the file exists, apply it: it can add sources and say which topics to emphasise or drop, and it overrides default behavior (the 32-item cap and the three categories stay). If it does not exist, proceed with the six default sources; nothing here is required. Setup, a smallest working PREFERENCES.md and the proof command are in [Setup.md](Setup.md). Run state is not config: it is written to `MEMORY/STATE/SecurityUpdates-last-check.json` (shape in `Intents/Update.md` § Tool contract).

## Sources

`sources.json` in the skill root is the one list of the six default sources: id, name, URL, type, and the categories each one feeds.

**Custom sources:** list them under "Extra sources" in `PREFERENCES.md` (see Data & Config); `sources.json` in the skill root holds the six defaults and is overwritten by updates, so do not edit it.

## Gotchas

- Not for stack-specific CVE tracking: use your own vulnerability-management tooling for that (a private overlay skill routes those requests on its own triggers). SecurityUpdates is for industry-wide security news.
- Research publications vs news: Distinguish between new research papers and news reporting. Cite appropriately.

## Examples

**"What's new in security?"** → Update intent → a ranked ≤32-item digest of what is new across all six sources since `~/.claude/LIFEOS/MEMORY/STATE/SecurityUpdates-last-check.json` was last written, and that state file updated for the next run.

**"/secupdates"** → same Update intent, slash-command entry.

**Second run same day** → only items whose keys are not already in the state file surface; an empty digest with "no new items since last check" is the correct result, not a failure.

# Shortcuts

Turn GUI-only macOS Shortcuts into callable LifeOS automation. Shortcuts reaches Apple-only surfaces (HomeKit/Home, native system actions, app intents) that have no other automation path. Computer use is slow and pixel-fragile, while the `shortcuts` CLI is fast and deterministic but can only run shortcuts, never build them. So each capability is built once (BuildShortcut) and is plain CLI from then on (RunShortcut, through `Tools/Shortcuts.ts`). This is CLI-first doctrine applied to the no-API problem.

## Ideal State

- Each Apple-only capability is built once as a Shortcut under the exact name its consumers call, and is proven by a `run` whose output matches the spec, never by how the editor looks.
- Every later use is plain CLI through `Tools/Shortcuts.ts` or `shortcuts run`, with no pixels and no computer use.
- A failed run or missing shortcut is diagnosed against the exact registered names, so a case or whitespace mismatch is caught before anything is rebuilt.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **BuildShortcut** | "build a shortcut", "create a shortcut", "set up the X shortcut" | `Intents/BuildShortcut.md` |
| **RunShortcut** | "run the X shortcut", "invoke X", any consumer calling a built shortcut | `Intents/RunShortcut.md` |
| **ListShortcuts** | "list shortcuts", "what shortcuts exist", "does X exist" | `Intents/ListShortcuts.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup, a worked example of adding your own shortcut, and the read-only proof commands |

## Gotchas

- **Creation is GUI-only: there is no `shortcuts create`.** The `shortcuts` CLI runs, lists, and views, but cannot author. Never claim a shortcut was "built" via CLI.
- **Name matching is exact, case and spaces included.** `shortcuts run "Casa Set Zone 1 Temp"` fails silently-ish (nonzero exit) if the registered name is `casa set zone 1 temp` or has a trailing space. Confirm with `exists` after building, register the exact string a consumer expects, and on a nonzero `run` with no clear error, diff the target string against `list` before rebuilding anything.
- **Input arrives on stdin; output is whatever the last action returns.** The CLI pipes `--input` to the shortcut's stdin and captures the final action's output on stdout; without a final output action, stdout comes back empty.

## Data & Config

The skill keeps no per-user data. Shortcut names belong to the consumer that calls them: a home-control skill, for example, builds its thermostat names from `thermostat_shortcut_prefix` and `thermostat_room` lines in its own `Config.md`. There is no config file for this skill. First-time setup, a worked example and a read-only proof: [Setup.md](Setup.md).

The frontmatter `evals` check (`list`) proves this skill on its own. A consumer that depends on a particular shortcut name can check it with `Tools/Shortcuts.ts exists "<name>"`, which exits 1 when that name is not registered.

## Examples

**Example 1: Build the thermostat status shortcut**
```
User: "build the thermostat status shortcut"
→ BuildShortcut, authored through Skill("ComputerUse", "Drive") --app Shortcuts
→ "<prefix> Thermostat Status" exists, reads every thermostat through Home actions,
  and `bun Tools/Shortcuts.ts run "<prefix> Thermostat Status"` returns
  "Zone 1 21 heating, Zone 2 20 idle"
```

**Example 2: A consumer runs a built shortcut**
```
A home-control skill's thermostat script calls `shortcuts run "<prefix> Set Zone 1 Temp"`
with "21" on stdin → RunShortcut path → deterministic, no computer use
```

**Example 3: Check what's there**
```
User: "do my <prefix> shortcuts exist yet?"
→ ListShortcuts: bun Tools/Shortcuts.ts list | rg "<prefix>"
→ the matching names, or a plain "not built yet"
```

---
name: Simplify

version: 1.0.1
description: "Research-first simplification of any file, skill, tool, subsystem or codebase against its ideal state: reads its ISA or derives its purpose, maps every dependent (callers, imports, references, hooks, settings, docs, tests), classifies each element with evidence as load-bearing, duplicate, dead, cruft or over-abstracted, then proposes and applies cuts that keep every behaviour a dependent relies on, proven by before-and-after parity checks. USE WHEN simplify, simplify this, simplify this system, remove cruft, remove duplication, dedupe, dead code, clean this up, this has gotten bloated, too complicated, reduce complexity, consolidate, strip this down without breaking it, what can we delete. NOT FOR always-on context files (Trim), cleanup of just the current diff (/simplify), harmony across many systems (Unify), auditing prompt rules for over-prompting (BitterLessonEngineering), bug hunting (/code-review)."
evals:
  manual:
    reason: "the claim that matters is that no behaviour a dependent relies on was lost, which only the target's own tests and probes can show, and those differ for every target"
    falsifier: "after an Apply run, a baseline check from the survey passes fewer cases than before, or a removed name still has a caller that a fresh reference search finds"
---

# Simplify

Simplify makes a target smaller and clearer without breaking anything that depends on it. A target can be a file, a skill, a tool, a subsystem or a whole repo. The work comes in three intents, each building on the record from the one before: Survey maps the target read-only, Propose ranks the cuts and holds them for a yes, and Apply lands the approved cuts with proven parity. The central rule: a cut never drops a behaviour that a dependent or ISA criterion relies on, and anything the evidence cannot explain stays. Records sit next to the target's ISA when there is one.

## Ideal State

- The target ends smaller and clearer, and every behaviour a dependent or ISA criterion relies on still works, shown by the same baseline checks passing before and after.
- No element is cut on looks: each cut rests on a survey finding with its searches cited, and anything the evidence cannot explain stays.
- Nothing changes until the principal approves the specific rows, and a delete of irreplaceable content gets its own yes.
- Each stage leaves its record under `LIFEOS/MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/simplify/`, so the next stage builds on evidence rather than on memory.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Survey** | "simplify X", "what can we delete", "map this before we cut", "is this dead" | `Intents/Survey.md` |
| **Propose** | "what would you cut", "propose the simplifications", follows Survey in the same run | `Intents/Propose.md` |
| **Apply** | "apply them", "y" or approved row numbers after a proposal | `Intents/Apply.md` |

A bare "simplify X" runs Survey and then Propose, and stops at the proposal. A Survey-only request, which is how a read-only analysis calls this skill, stops at the survey.

## Data & Config

None. This skill reads no config and needs no account or key. Each stage writes its record under `LIFEOS/MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/simplify/` next to the target's ISA, if it has one; nothing else is created.

## Gotchas

- **Zero code-search hits does not mean dead.** LifeOS calls a great deal of code by string: hook registrations in `settings.json`, launchd plists, workflow YAML, skill routing tables, spawned commands and dynamic imports. `ReferenceCheck.ts --shipped-paths` exists because plain path scans missed spawn and dynamic-import specifiers.
- **The file can change mid-run.** Memory loops and peer sessions write to the same trees. A file edited after its survey is re-read before it is touched (Trim, where a concurrent deploy-command fix was nearly reverted).

## Examples

**Example 1: Simplify a tool**
```
User: "simplify LIFEOS/TOOLS/ReferenceCheck.ts"
→ Survey intent, then Propose
→ Purpose from its header and DocCheck lineage, every caller, findings per function, test baseline
→ A ranked table of cuts, each with its parity check, held for y
```

**Example 2: Land the approved cuts**
```
User: "y, but skip 4"
→ Apply intent
→ Rows 1–3 and 5 land as separate commits, tests show the same pass count before and after, and the measured reduction sits beside the estimate
```

**Example 3: An always-on context file**
```
User: "simplify CLAUDE.md"
→ Routed to Trim, which owns always-on context files and their directive-coverage gate
```

# Speaking

Discovers and tracks paid speaking opportunities that fit the topics you list in Config.md. FindOpportunities scrapes conference CFPs and monitors speaker pages, then updates the opportunities list; ShowOpportunities analyzes fit, prioritizes by urgency, and returns recommendations with CFP deadlines; ProposeTalks drafts talk and panel proposals to send an organizer. Paid speaking slots get filled months ahead and the good ones close their CFPs quietly; miss the deadline and the opportunity is gone for a year, so the skill watches the sources, keeps a running list, and flags what fits and what is about to close.

**Topics (the fit test for every intent):** the `## Topics` list in Config.md (§ Data & Config). An event listed under `## Excluded events` there is never tracked or recommended, whatever its fit.

**Urgency windows (every intent):** Immediate (urgent) means the CFP or submission closes within 14 days, or is rolling; High Priority means it closes in 15-30 days; Worth Watching means it closes later or the CFP is not open yet.

## Ideal State

- The tracked list holds only paid (or flagged very-high-prestige) opportunities that fit the Config.md topics, each with its CFP close date, pay tier and next action. Unpaid community meetups appear only when the user asks for them.
- Nothing closes unnoticed: deadlines inside the Immediate window surface as urgent, and past events move to the archive with their outcome instead of disappearing.
- Every recommendation is specific to its opportunity, carries its submission deadline, and carries a URL or contact to act on.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **FindOpportunities** | "find speaking opportunities", "update speaking list", "check speaking sources" | `Intents/FindOpportunities.md` |
| **ShowOpportunities** | "show me opportunities", "what speaking opportunities", "analyze speaking list", "where should I speak" | `Intents/ShowOpportunities.md` |
| **ProposeTalks** | "propose talks", "talk ideas for a conference", "panel topics", "what could I speak on" | `Intents/ProposeTalks.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup, what Config.md holds, adding your own sources, a scheduled deadline check, proving the skill works |
| `Sources.md` | the kinds of source to check (speaker pages, conferences, bureaus, CFP aggregators), what each yields, and how often; the actual sources are in Config.md |
| `Tools/CheckOpportunities.ts` | checking the opportunities list for entries missing a close date, a URL or contact, or a pay tier, and for past deadlines left outside Archive (`--json`, `--today YYYY-MM-DD`, optional list path; exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 unreadable) |
| `Patterns/` | `recommend_talkpanel_topics/system.md` is the system prompt ProposeTalks runs to turn the speaker's goals, positions and interests into talk or panel proposals for an organizer |

## Data & Config

First-time setup, the Config.md fields, accounts and a proof command: [Setup.md](Setup.md). configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`. If Config.md is missing, stop and point the user at Setup.md; never guess topics, fees or sources.

- **Config:** `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Speaking/Config.md` holds `## Topics`, `## Fee range`, `## Excluded events`, `## Speaker record` (where goals, positions and credentials come from), `## Signature talking points`, `## Highest-yield source`, `## Speaker pages to monitor`, `## Conferences` (by pay tier, plus priority targets), `## Speaker bureaus` and `## Extra CFP aggregators`.
- **Opportunities list:** `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Speaking/Opportunities.md`, written by FindOpportunities and read by the other intents. Created on the first run when absent.

## Gotchas

- None recorded yet.

## Examples

```
User: "Find speaking opportunities"
→ FindOpportunities
→ The opportunities list gains the new finds, and the user gets what's new, what closes within two weeks, and what was archived
```

```
User: "Update the speaking list"
→ FindOpportunities
→ An incremental update since the last run: new opportunities added, expired ones archived with their outcome
```

```
User: "Show me opportunities"
→ ShowOpportunities
→ Opportunities bucketed by urgency and fit, each with its deadline, pay tier and one specific next step
```

```
User: "Propose some talks for Example Engineering Summit"
→ ProposeTalks
→ Three talk abstracts and three panel topics fitted to that event, ready to paste to the organizer
```

# Spotify

Acts on the principal's real Spotify account through `Tools/Spotify.ts` — a deterministic CLI that calls the Spotify Web API directly. No MCP, no server process, no session registration: any session can invoke it via Bash immediately.

```bash
bun ~/.claude/skills/Spotify/Tools/Spotify.ts <command> [flags]   # --help for the full list
```

## Ideal State

- Every requested account change (follow, playlist build, library read, queue, playback) is one `Tools/Spotify.ts` call keyed by IDs or URIs, and the account state afterwards matches the request.
- Auth is set up once and never repeated by hand: tokens refresh per invocation, and a dead token or redirect mismatch is traced to its real fix (re-run `auth`, or fix the dashboard URI).
- Playback is attempted only on a Premium account with an active device, so a Free account still gets search, playlists and library.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Authorize** | "set up spotify", "authorize spotify", "connect spotify", auth broken | `Intents/Authorize.md` |
| **Manage** | play / search / playlists / queue / library ops | `Intents/Manage.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time install: the developer app, the three `.env` keys, the proof command |
| `Tools/` | `Spotify.help.md` is the full flag reference (same as `--help`); `EnvText.ts` is the pure env-file helper `Spotify.ts` writes tokens with |

## Data & Config

This skill reads no files under `LIFEOS/USER/`. Credentials are env-only: `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` and `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` in `~/.claude/.env` (names only here, never values). First-time setup, the Spotify developer app and the proof command are in [Setup.md](Setup.md). Tokens auto-refresh per invocation; a missing refresh token means run `Intents/Authorize.md`. With the credentials missing, the tool exits 1 and points at Setup.md.

## Gotchas

- **`search` works before user auth** (client-credentials fallback); every other command needs the refresh token.
- **401 on every call** → the refresh token died (password change, revoked access); re-run `auth` (`Intents/Authorize.md`). The tool persists rotated refresh tokens automatically.
- **`/me/playlists` returns `tracks: null` on playlist rows (observed)** — never assume `tracks.total` exists; the CLI omits the count when absent.

## Examples

- "Add this playlist link to my Spotify" → Manage → the playlist is followed with `follow-playlist --id <ID>` (ID from the URL) and shows in `playlists`.
- "Make me a focus-music playlist and fill it" → Manage → a new playlist from `create-playlist`, holding the tracks `search` resolved, added with `add-tracks`.
- "What's playing?" → Manage → the `now-playing` result.
- "Skip this / turn it down" → Manage → `next` / `volume --percent 30` on the active Premium device.

description: State journaling from shorthand like M4, H2, CF5 (H overall, M mood, E energy, S sleep, R relationships, F financial, C creativity, CF creative freedom, W workout, K walk, A affirmation) on 1-5, with freshness resets. USE WHEN a message is only dimension shorthand (M4, e4 cf3, W, K, A), log my state, log my mood, state check-in, how am I tracking, just worked out, went for a walk, did my affirmations. NOT FOR life-goal percentages (use `Telos`), health imports, macOS stats (Vitals).
---

# StateLog

**Contents:** Ideal State · Intent Routing · The grammar · Data & Config · Tool contract · Gotchas · Examples

Two keystrokes to a durable journal entry. The user sends `M2` on any channel; it lands timestamped in the state log and the statusline reflects it. The point is zero-friction capture of mood and state so correlations (mood vs sleep vs workouts) become computable later.

## Ideal State

- Every entry the user states lands in the log in one tool call and gets one short acknowledgment, with no follow-up questions or analysis.
- Ratings come only from the user's own words; inferred events reset freshness counters and never write a rating.
- A status read shows each dimension's latest value and age, and names what is stale or never logged in one line.
- The journal stays the user's: it lives under `LIFEOS/USER/STATE/` and never enters this skill or any public artifact.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Log** | A shorthand entry, "log my state/mood", "just worked out", "went for a walk" | `Intents/Log.md` |
| **Status** | "current state", "state check-in", "how am I tracking" | `Intents/Status.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup, or `Config.md` is missing |
| `EvalState.md` | checking the `state-shorthand` eval suite's latest scores (machine-owned, never hand-edited) |

## The grammar

`<Letter><Digit 1-5>` plus optional note (`M2 slept badly`). Bare `W` or `K` resets that freshness counter.

| Letter | Dimension | Kind |
|--------|-----------|------|
| H | overall | rating 1-5 |
| M | mood | rating 1-5 |
| E | energy | rating 1-5 |
| S | sleep | rating 1-5 |
| R | relationships | rating 1-5 |
| F | financial | rating 1-5 |
| C | overall creativity | rating 1-5 |
| CF | creative freedom | rating 1-5 |
| W | workout | freshness (days-since) |
| K | walk | freshness (days-since) |
| A | affirmation | freshness (days-since) |

Scale (star-rating semantics, higher is better): 1 really bad · 2 bad · 3 fine (shown yellow, never treated as a crisis) · 4 and 5 the preferred range (shown green). The parser clamps 0/6-9 into range and preserves the raw value. Every dimension reads the same direction — there are no inverted dimensions.

## Data & Config

What each dimension means to the user, where the creativity pair's framing comes from, the affirmation practice file, and the workout signal source: `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/StateLog/Config.md` (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). First-time setup is in [Setup.md](Setup.md). Read it when discussing the creativity pair, logging an `A`, or deciding whether an event counts as a workout signal. Logging itself works without it; when Config.md is missing, say so once, point the user at `Setup.md`, skip the streak bump and signal resets, and still log the entry. The letters and 1-5 scale are the tool's defaults in `State.ts`; Config.md only records what they mean to the user.

## Tool contract

The deterministic engine is `~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts` (cross-consumer: statusline, interview, this skill):

```bash
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts log "M4"              # rate
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts log "M2 rough day"    # rate + note
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts log "W"               # freshness reset
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts log "H5" --source interview
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts reset W               # signal-driven reset
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts current [--json]      # snapshot with freshness tiers
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts statusline            # compact segment
bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/State.ts rebuild               # re-derive current.json from log
```

Data: `LIFEOS/USER/STATE/log.jsonl` (append-only) + `current.json` (derived). The statusline reads `current.json` directly with jq — never spawn the tool from render paths.

## Gotchas

- A bare rating letter with no digit (`M`) is an error, not a default — only W/K/A accept bare-letter resets.
- Bare `A` = "did today's affirmation reps". Config.md names the practice file (`Affirmation practice file`); on an `A` entry, also bump the streak line in that file's Active section. With no practice file configured, log the `A` and touch nothing else.
- `--source` records where an entry came from, for later correlation: `manual` (default), `interview`, `signal`. `reset W|K` stamps `signal` itself, so an entry inferred from an event ("just worked out") goes through `reset` (Intents/Log.md), never through `log` with a hand-passed source.
- Freshness is per-dimension, three tiers (fresh/aging/stale) with windows declared in `State.ts` `DIMENSIONS`: mood and energy decay in hours, relationships and financial in days. `State.ts current` computes each tier; a stale dimension is the prompt to log, not an error.
- Entries are case-insensitive, and a message may carry several at once (`e4 cf3` = energy 4, creative freedom 3). A message that is nothing but shorthand routes here silently.
- Don't route goal-percentage talk here: "health 68%" is a life-goal gap score, not a journal entry.

## Examples

```
User: "e4 cf3"
→ Log intent
→ Energy 4 and creative freedom 3 are in the log; the reply is one acknowledgment line

User: "just worked out"
→ Log intent
→ The workout counter resets with source signal, and no rating is written

User: "how am I tracking"
→ Status intent
→ A snapshot of each dimension's value and age, closing on one line that names what is stale
```

name: Statvs
version: 1.0.1
description: "Front door to STATVS (said status), the one append-only record of what happened across LifeOS and every app it runs: checks the record's health, says whether a system, app or site reports into it, writes rows, answers what happened, rebuilds and drills views, rewinds and replays past turns, and onboards a system through the five-step migration. USE WHEN statvs, status logging, status record, the record, is X logging to status, is my site reporting into status, full status logging, log this to status, write a status row, what happened, status tail, verify the record, status counters, drill, restore drill, rebuild a view, compare a view, rewind a turn, replay a miss, onboard X into status, migrate X to statvs, dual-write, register a stream. metadata:
  short-description: "Check, query, write to and onboard systems onto STATVS, the one append-only record of state for LifeOS and its apps, said status."
evals:
  deterministic:
    - command: "bun LIFEOS/STATVS/Statvs.ts verify --json"
      falsifier: "prints ok:false with a non-empty problems list when any segment's hash chain, seal or anchor fails"
---

# Statvs

STATVS (Roman spelling, said "status") is the one record of what happened across LifeOS and every app it runs. Things that happened are appended once as rows and never rewritten; every other piece of state is a view folded from those rows that can be deleted and rebuilt. When the principal says "status logging", "the record" or "is X reporting into status", this skill is what they mean, and every intent here answers from the record and its CLI, never from a system's private log. Shared facts the intents rely on:

- **Concept:** `LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Statvs/StatvsSystem.md`. **Criteria and build state:** `LIFEOS/STATVS/ISA.md` (maintainer-side; may be absent on an install). **Engine:** `LIFEOS/STATVS/` with CLI `Statvs.ts`, `Rewind.ts`, and the stream registry `streams.ts`.
- **Row shape:** one envelope (`id`, `seq`, `hlc`, `ts`, `writer`, `stream`, `class`, `app`, `kind`, `severity`, `title`, `session`, `ref`, `data`, chain fields). An append to a stream not in `streams.ts` is refused.
- **Privacy classes** (`public`, `system`, `personal`, `customer`) are the first directory of every segment and never share a file. Secret-shaped values are refused at the writer; tenant content never enters the record.
- **Reporting in** means rows from that system are landing in the record under its own `writer`, on registered streams, today. A system that only writes its own log, or only reaches Vigil through an adapter, is not reporting in.
- **Migration** happens one system at a time in five steps: dual-write, build the view from each store, compare until equal, switch every reader, delete the old store. A system has moved only when its old store is gone.
- **Neighbors:** Vigil is the advocate that reads the record and decides what to tell the principal; its `writeEvent` path also lands rows in the `event` stream, so posting a notice-worthy event stays a Vigil job. Cortex curates what is worth remembering. The bare `s` / "status" shortcut is session status, not STATVS.

## Ideal State

- Every answer about the record, a system's coverage or what happened is grounded in output from `Statvs.ts` or `Rewind.ts` run this turn, and names the command it came from.
- "Is X reporting into STATVS" always gets a yes, partial or no verdict per required stream (at least deploy and app-health for a live app), with the writer names and last row time, or the absence, as evidence.
- Nothing the skill does weakens the record: no edit to a segment, no prune of a `forever` stream, no deleted old store before its view compares equal and the restore drill passed that day.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Status** | "statvs status", "is the record healthy", "verify the record", "status counters", "drill loss", "how far is the migration" | `Intents/Status.md` |
| **Coverage** | "is X logging to status", "is my site reporting into status", "full status logging for X", "what reports into statvs" | `Intents/Coverage.md` |
| **Append** | "log this to status", "write a status row", "record this in statvs" | `Intents/Append.md` |
| **Query** | "what happened", "status tail", "show the rows for X", "when did X last report" | `Intents/Query.md` |
| **Rebuild** | "rebuild a view", "compare a view", "run the drill", "restore drill", "back up the record" | `Intents/Rebuild.md` |
| **Rewind** | "rewind a turn", "replay a miss", "rebuild that turn", "prove the fix on the old failure" | `Intents/Rewind.md` |
| **Onboard** | "onboard X into status", "migrate X to statvs", "make X report into status", "register a stream", "dual-write X" | `Intents/Onboard.md` |

## Gotchas

- **`drill` loss counts every unclaimed STATE file, not lost data.** A large loss number is mostly files under `MEMORY/STATE/` that no registered view claims yet. It measures migration distance; read `unclaimed_by_dir` and the per-view `equal` flags before calling anything broken.
- **A view marked `unmaterialized` has never been written, so it compares unequal.** `rebuild <view>` once materializes it; that is not a mismatch in the data.
- **`counters.refused` is a running total since the counters file was created, not today's refusals.** Report it as a total, and look at `tail` for what was refused recently.
- **The `event` stream is written by Vigil's `writeEvent`, not by `Statvs.ts append`.** Appending a notice-worthy row straight to `event` skips Vigil's validation and dedup; use `Statvs.ts event` or Vigil's Emit.
- **"Is it working" starts with `Statvs.ts reconcile`, not `verify`.** `verify` proves the rows that exist are intact; only reconcile finds rows that should exist and do not (missed turns, unrecorded refusals, an unshipped backlog, drifted schedules). `--hours 24` widens the window; without `--emit` it only reads. The hourly `statvs-reconcile` workflow posts each gap to Vigil.
- **The cloud record answers by default.** `tail`, `reconcile`, `tools/Coverage.ts` and `Rewind.ts` read Cloudflare through `lib/cloudRead.ts`; `--local` reads this Mac's segments until they are retired (migration ISA F9). The `rg` lines in the intents' tool contracts search the local segments and miss nothing only while those still exist. `compare-cloud --days N` proves the two agree. Cloud `tail` prints cloud rows (with `offset`, `chain`, `machine`, `srcHash`, and no `hash` or `prev`) and widens its window until it has `--n` rows. Rows of `ship: false` streams (`observe`) exist only on the machine that wrote them; the cloud holds a `local-only` marker and, once `seal-copies` has run, a sealed ciphertext copy of each row.
- **The `s` shortcut and the word "status" collide.** "Status" alone, with no mention of logging, a record, a system reporting in or STATVS, is the session-status shortcut.

## Examples

**Example 1: Is a site reporting in**
```
User: "Do we have full status logging enabled for my site?"
→ Coverage intent
→ Per-stream verdict (deploy, app-health, review) with writer names and last row times, or "no rows" for each missing one, and the Onboard step that would close the gap
```

**Example 2: Health of the record**
```
User: "Is statvs healthy?"
→ Status intent
→ verify result, counters, drill loss with what it means, and which systems sit at which migration step
```

**Example 3: Prove a fix on a past miss**
```
User: "Replay the turn behind errata 412 with the new guard"
→ Rewind intent
→ Fixture built with Rewind.ts, Assay.ts replay result saying whether the miss flipped, and which tier of proof that is
```

NOT FOR multi-source research (Research), writing original social posts or blog drafts, wisdom extraction (ExtractWisdom).

# StoryExplanation

Turns any source (a YouTube video, a URL, a file, pasted text, or "this" for the current conversation) into a narrative explanation in the user's own first-person voice. It explores 5-7 framings, picks the strongest, and outputs in the format you ask for: a 3-part narrative, a links version with inline citations, a 5-line abridged version, or a numbered CSE/CSE5. Each point stands alone, so any one can be lifted straight to social media.

Every intent reads the source the same way. A YouTube URL (contains "youtube.com" or "youtu.be") is fetched with `fabric -y <URL>`, any other URL (starts with http:// or https://) with `fabric -u <URL>`, a file path by reading the file, pasted text as given, and previous output or "this" from the conversation.

Every format has a deterministic check. `bun skills/StoryExplanation/Tools/CheckFormat.ts --format <format> [--lines N] [--words N]` reads the output from stdin or `--file`, exits 0 when it conforms and 1 with one violation per line when it does not; flags and per-format checks are in `Tools/CheckFormat.help.md`. It checks counts, numbering, headers, bullets, labels, periods, link placement and the default cliche list, never voice or fidelity.

| Intent | `--format` | Other flags |
|---|---|---|
| Create | `create` | none |
| CreateWithLinks | `links` | `--lines N` when the request named a length |
| CreateAbridged | `abridged` | none |
| Cse | `cse` | `--lines N`, and `--words N` when the request named a word count |
| Cse5 | `cse5` | none |

## Ideal State

- Every explanation is written in the user's first-person voice from the voice file and notes named in Config.md (the generic defaults when it is absent), never in the assistant's own register or another person's voice.
- The source was actually read before writing (a YouTube transcript through `fabric -y`, a web page through `fabric -u`, a file, pasted text or the conversation), and nothing in the explanation goes beyond it.
- The output is exactly the format and length the request named, with no commentary around it (`Tools/CheckFormat.ts` exits 0 on it), and each point or sentence is a complete thought that lifts to social media unedited.
- Several framings were explored, the explanation uses the one picked as strongest over the others, and someone who never saw the source can follow the idea from the explanation alone.
- When Config.md names an opinion-lookup command, the explanation agrees with the user's published position on the topic as that command reports it.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Create** | "story explanation", default | `Intents/Create.md` |
| **CreateWithLinks** | "with links", "with sources" | `Intents/CreateWithLinks.md` |
| **CreateAbridged** | "abridged", "5-12 words per line" | `Intents/CreateAbridged.md` |
| **Cse** | "CSE", "comprehensive", `/cse`; where an install adds line-count shortcut commands, they call this intent with that line count | `Intents/Cse.md` |
| **Cse5** | "CSE5", "5 lines", `/cse5` | `Intents/Cse5.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `VoiceStyleGuide.md` | how the user's voice is applied, cliches to avoid |
| `NarrativeFraming.md` | Framing selection rule + angle palette |
| `OutputFormats.md` | choosing between the formats |
| `Patterns/` | the Create intent's 3-part narrative prompt (`Patterns/create_story_explanation/system.md`) |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup of Config.md and the voice file |
| `Tools/` | checking an output against its format (`CheckFormat.ts`; flags in `CheckFormat.help.md`) |
| `EvalState.md` | the storyexplanation-cse eval scores (machine-owned by `skills/Assay/Tools/EvalState.ts`, never hand-edited) |

## Data & Config

The user's voice and optional integrations live in `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/StoryExplanation/Config.md`; first-time setup is in [Setup.md](Setup.md). The user reviews and owns anything posted under their name.

# StoryFilm

A story goes in; a verified film of it comes out. One creative stage (the storyboard) and a deterministic tail (bible, shots, narration, render, verification, critique, delivery).

## Ideal State

- A story file becomes a film a viewer accepts as one made thing: the same faces first frame to last, each painting fitting its beat, the caption in step with the voice.
- Every film is read back before anyone sees it: `Out/verify.json` green and complete, the Assay video eval set (`video-eval`) passed in the verify stage as `Intents/Produce.md` declares it, the review sheets looked at, and the ArtDirection critique passed on the exact bytes delivered.
- Nothing reaches the principal as a first draft: the film and its sheets land in the downloads folder only through `Run.ts --deliver`, after a passing critique and a Proof receipt.
- Expensive stages run once per change: the storyboard is reviewed and linted before any painting, and every later stage is hash-cached so an edit redoes only what it touched.
- Nothing leaves review: the skill has no upload or publish path.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Full** | "film this story", "animated reading of X", "turn this story into a movie", anything that starts from a story file | `Intents/Full.md` |
| **Storyboard** | "storyboard this", "write the bible", "plan the shots", a redo of the creative stage after intake | `Intents/Storyboard.md` |
| **Produce** | "paint the shots", "render it", "re-render after an edit", "verify the film" | `Intents/Produce.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `References/StoryboardSchema.md` | writing or editing `Storyboard.json` |
| `ISA.md` | changing what the skill does: its ideal state, criteria and decisions |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: Fish Audio and Google keys, ffmpeg and the other programs, optional Config.json |

`Full` is Intake → Storyboard → Produce. The storyboard is the review checkpoint when the principal wants one: it is cheap to change and forty paintings are not. Skip it by saying so ("straight through").

## Run Layout

```
<run>/
  run.json  Beats.json  Storyboard.json  pronunciations.json (optional)
  Bible/<id>.<hash>.png        style plate + reference sheets
  Shots/<beat>.<hash>.png      one painting per beat · contact-sheet.png
  Narration/<beat>.<hash>.{mp3,align.json,wav}  narration.wav  timeline.json
  Out/composition/             the HyperFrames project Build.ts writes (index.html, plan.js, film.js, shots/, narration.wav)
  Out/film.mp4  render.json  render.log  verify.json  Critique.json  frames/  caption-check/  review/{contact-sheet,motion-strip}.png
```

## Data & Config

First-time setup (accounts, keys, files to fill in): [Setup.md](Setup.md).

- Voice: `--voice`, else the story's `audio_voice` frontmatter, else the DA's main voice from `LIFEOS_CONFIG.toml`. The value is a role (`main`, `presenter`, `principal`), `fish:<reference id>`, or the `voice_id` of a `[da.voices.*]` profile that has a `fish_reference_id`; any other id stops with an error naming where to add one. Narration is Fish Audio Drama 3 (`FishTTS.ts`) and takes no model flag; the DA's own voice reads at its configured `fish_speed`, any other voice at natural pace. Key: `FISH_API_KEY` in the env file; the `principal` role also needs `FISH_PRINCIPAL_VOICE_ID`.
- Images: the `geminiImage` lane in `LIFEOS/TOOLS/models.ts` on `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, 16:9 at 2K, reference images attached per shot.
- `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/StoryFilm/Config.json`: `runsRoot` (default `~/StoryFilms`; `LIFEOS_STORYFILM_DIR` overrides), `fonts.serif` / `fonts.serifItalic` (paths to licensed faces; `path.ttc#<index>` names one face of a collection), embedded into each composition as @font-face data. No font configured means the default serif, Source Serif 4 roman and italic (SIL Open Font License), installed by `Setup.ts` as the pinned `@fontsource/source-serif-4` dependency.
- `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/StoryFilm/PREFERENCES.md`: the principal's casting and register taste for the Storyboard intent. `Config.json` `provingRun` names the run slug the skill ISA's proving-run checks use (`Setup.ts --proving-run` prints it).
- Pronunciations: `USER/PRINCIPAL/PRONUNCIATIONS.json` plus a per-run `pronunciations.json`, applied to spoken text only; the caption shows the story's words.
- `Run.ts` refuses a run dir under the config tree or the user-data repo (symlinks dereferenced first).

## Gotchas

- **The image model copies whatever is in the style plate, including things that are not style (2026-09-17, first run).** A violet dot in the plate put a stray bead on a character sheet. Keep the plate's subject empty (the prompt asks for an empty interior) and say in each bible desc what the character must NOT carry.
- **The story file can change under a run.** Intake reads the frontmatter once; a voice or prose edit in the source after intake is invisible until `Intake.ts` runs again (2026-09-17: the narrator was re-cast in the story file after the first intake, and the first film went out in the old voice). Re-run Intake before any re-narration and diff the beat count.
- **`bun test <bare path>` drops child-process output (Bun 1.3.6).** Always `bun test ./skills/StoryFilm/Tools`.

## Examples

**Example 1: a story file to a film**
```
User: "Turn the story at stories/the-lighthouse.md into an animated reading"
→ Full: Intake writes Beats.json; the Storyboard intent writes the bible and one shot per beat; lint exits 0
→ Run.ts: bible painted, shots painted (4 at a time, cached by hash), narration synthesized, film rendered, verify.json green, review sheets written
→ ArtDirection critique of Out/film.mp4 passes into Out/Critique.json; Run.ts --from sheet --deliver lands the film and sheets in the downloads folder
```

**Example 2: one painting is wrong**

```
User: "The kitchen in beat 12 looks like a restaurant — fix it"
→ Edit that shot's prompt in Storyboard.json (and the place's bible desc if the sheet is the problem)
→ Run.ts --from lint --to shots repaints that one beat (everything else is cached); Run.ts --from build re-renders and re-verifies
```

```
→ Tighten her bible desc (age, face), Characters.ts --only ana repaints her sheet, Shots.ts --force repaints the shots that carry her ref (their hash changed with the sheet)
```

USE WHEN Stripe, subscriptions, billing, MRR, revenue, customers, invoices, refund, coupon, payment link, charges, subscriber count, earnings. # Stripe Billing Operations

**Contents:** Ideal State · Intent Routing · Data & Config · Tool contract · Gotchas · Examples

Answers and acts on Stripe billing questions: promotion codes and coupons, products and prices, subscriptions and subscriber counts, MRR and revenue, customers, payments, invoices, refunds and payment links, across one main account and any number of additional ones. With more than one Stripe account, using the wrong key returns wrong numbers silently, so every call names the account's key.

## Ideal State

- Every figure comes from the account the user meant, through that account's env var, with keys loaded from `~/.claude/.env` and never printed or hardcoded; a missing Config.md or `STRIPE_SDK_DIR` stops the run with a pointer to `Setup.md` instead of a guess.
- Counts and revenue cover every page of the list they come from, and historical views keep canceled and churned subscriptions and attribute every row to a product.
- No write reaches Stripe without the user's explicit approval, and every write reports the resulting object back.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **ListProducts** | "products", "what products", "list products" | `Intents/ListProducts.md` |
| **Subscriptions** | "subscriptions", "subscribers", "how many subscribers" | `Intents/Subscriptions.md` |
| **Revenue** | "revenue", "MRR", "how much", "earnings", "income" | `Intents/Revenue.md` |
| **Customers** | "customers", "customer list", "who subscribes" | `Intents/Customers.md` |
| **Payments** | "payments", "recent payments", "charges" | `Intents/Payments.md` |
| **Manage** | "promotion codes", "promo code", "find a coupon", "create product", "create price", "change the price", "cancel", "refund", "coupon", "invoice", "payment link" | `Intents/Manage.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: Config.md, `STRIPE_SDK_DIR`, the per-account key env vars, and the check that it works |

## Data & Config

Account-specific values — the SDK working directory (`STRIPE_SDK_DIR`), account aliases and their env var names, product and price IDs, product domains, invoicing practice, and the optional admin-dashboard endpoints — live in `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Stripe/Config.md`. First-time setup is in [Setup.md](Setup.md). Secrets are env-var names only, values in `~/.claude/.env`. The skill body is generic.

When Config.md is missing, or it names no `STRIPE_SDK_DIR`, stop, say so, and point the user at `Setup.md`. Never guess an SDK directory, an account, or a product list.

| Account | Env var | Format | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------|-------|
| **Main** (default) | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | `sk_live_*` | Used when no alias is given |
| **Additional** | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_<ALIAS>` | `sk_live_*` or restricted `rk_live_*` | Config.md's Accounts table maps each alias to its env var |

- **Test mode:** a test-mode key (`sk_test_*`) is its own row in the Accounts table, for example alias `test` with `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST`, used as `--account test`.
- **SDK:** `stripe` npm package (v20+), called with the API version Config.md names (the preamble below passes it).
- **Admin dashboard (optional):** if Config.md names an admin dashboard that serves cached Stripe endpoints (its base URL, the endpoint list and what each returns), prefer those for fast overview answers: customer and subscription totals, MRR, products with subscriber counts, monthly revenue, recent payments. Treat the cache as possibly minutes old and say so when freshness matters. With no dashboard configured, answer from the SDK; nothing else in this skill depends on it.

## Tool contract

**Reads go through the read-only CLI first:** `bun ~/.claude/LIFEOS/TOOLS/StripeRead.ts promos | coupons | products | prices | subs | customer <email> | balance | get <v1 path> [k=v…]` (`--account <alias>` for an additional account). It is a single plain command with no write path, so it runs wherever a shell command can, including unattended sessions. The inline `cd … && bun --env-file … -e` script below is arbitrary code, and a harness that asks before running such code will stop on it when nobody is there to approve, so use it only for writes and anything the CLI can't express, such as the computed reports in each intent. Two limits of the CLI, from its code: `products` and `prices` return active objects only, and every list stops at 1,000 rows, so a count of exactly 1,000 is a floor and needs `fetchAll` below.

Writes and computed reports run inside this preamble. Fill its two `<…>` values from Config.md before running it: the SDK folder (`STRIPE_SDK_DIR`, a directory where the `stripe` npm package is installed, with a leading `~` written as `$HOME`) and the API version (`STRIPE_API_VERSION`). `bun -e` resolves the SDK from that folder. If Config.md lacks either, stop and point at `Setup.md`. Each intent's Tool contract gives the body that replaces the last two lines.

```bash
cd "<STRIPE_SDK_DIR from Config.md>" && bun --env-file ~/.claude/.env -e "
import Stripe from 'stripe';
const API_VERSION = '<STRIPE_API_VERSION from Config.md>';
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, { apiVersion: API_VERSION });

async function fetchAll(listFn, params = {}) {
  const items = [];
  let hasMore = true;
  let startingAfter;
  while (hasMore) {
    const batch = await listFn({ limit: 100, ...params, ...(startingAfter ? { starting_after: startingAfter } : {}) });
    items.push(...batch.data);
    hasMore = batch.has_more;
    if (batch.data.length > 0) startingAfter = batch.data[batch.data.length - 1].id;
  }
  return items;
}

const result = await stripe.METHOD;
console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
"
```

For an additional account the key line becomes `const stripe = new Stripe(process.env['<ENV VAR>'], { apiVersion: API_VERSION });`, with `<ENV VAR>` taken from that alias's row in Config.md's Accounts table, never built from the alias by hand. The read-only CLIs (`StripeRead.ts`, `InvoiceWatch.ts`) resolve `--account <alias>` to `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_<ALIAS in capitals>`, so name each additional key that way. Bun's `--env-file` loads the configured key into the process without reading or printing the secret in shell. A restricted key (`rk_live_*`) allows only the scopes granted on it: read operations work; write operations (create/refund/cancel) fail unless that scope was granted.

## Gotchas

- **Daily product attribution must follow realized balance activity, not MRR.** Join each charge/refund/dispute balance transaction to its charge, then invoice or Checkout line items, price, and product; allocate multi-product invoices proportionally and retain unmatched activity as `Unattributed`. Report gross, refunds/adjustments, Stripe fees, and net using day boundaries in the timezone recorded in Config.md.
- **Invoice-generated charges may return `invoice: null`.** In recent API versions, a charge can expose only a description such as `Invoice ABCD1234-0001`. Recover the invoice with `/v1/invoices/search` by exact invoice number, then resolve `lines.data[].pricing.price_details.product`. Do not use the invoice description itself as the product name. Nested expansion of `lines.data.pricing.price_details.product` may be rejected; plain invoice retrieval already returns the product ID, which can be retrieved separately.

## Examples

```
User: "list active promotion codes in the main account"
→ Manage intent, read-only
→ A table of every active code with its coupon terms, redemptions and expiry
```

```
User: "cancel the annual subscription for customer X at period end"
→ Manage intent
→ After approval, the subscription shows cancel_at_period_end and the date access ends
```

```
User: "what's the MRR looking like?"
→ Revenue intent
→ MRR and ARR from every active subscription, labelled active-only and list price before discounts, with the count of discounted subscriptions, plus three months of gross, refunds, fees and net
```

# StudioLights

Deterministic control of a studio lighting rig through amaran Desktop's local WebSocket API (`ws://127.0.0.1:33782/ws`, protocol v2 — the same local API the official Bitfocus Companion module uses). The tool auto-launches amaran Desktop if it isn't running.

## Ideal State

- Every lighting change runs through `Tools/Lights.ts` against the rig the USER tree's `devices.json` and `scenes.json` define; no fixture, name or level is assumed from this skill.
- Done is said only when the lights themselves read back the requested state.
- A saved scene restores exactly the levels saved under its name, whether "recording", "normal" or any later caller asks for it.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Control** | "recording", "set the lights", "light scene", "dim X", "save this lighting" | `Intents/Control.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: amaran Desktop, finding node IDs, and writing `devices.json` and `scenes.json` |

## Data & Config

The rig lives in the USER tree, never in this skill: `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/StudioLights/devices.json` holds each fixture's name, node ID, model and whether it has color temperature, and `scenes.json` holds the saved scenes. Free-form notes about the rig (where each light stands, what each scene is for, which Shortcut or macro calls a scene by name) go in `Config.md` in the same folder; the tool never reads it. First-time setup, including how to find node IDs and a worked example of a voice trigger, is in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

`Tools/Lights.ts` exits with an error pointing at Setup.md when `devices.json` is missing; `Lights.ts devices` lists the node IDs to put in it and runs before the file exists. The tool finds that folder from its own skill folder's name, so the skill folder and its USER folder must share a name.

## Gotchas

- amaran Desktop must be running, because it is the bridge between the Mac and the lights' Bluetooth mesh. `Lights.ts` launches it and waits up to 30s. If it opens signed out, it reports no lights; sign in once in its window.
- Daylight-only lights report `cct: 0` and ignore color-temperature writes. Mark them `"supportsCct": false` in `devices.json` and the tool skips CCT for them; `Lights.ts devices` guesses this for you.
- The API's intensity unit is 0–1000, ten per percent. The tool takes 0–100 and converts.
- Each light accepts one command per 200ms. The tool spaces writes 220ms apart, so a scene takes about half a second per light. Do not run writes in parallel.
- Each request carries a token in the same AES-GCM format the official Bitfocus Companion module sends; `Lights.ts` builds it for every request.
- amaran Desktop is the only automation path; the phone apps for these lights offer none.
- Anything that calls a scene by name (a Shortcut, a macro, another skill) breaks silently when the scene is renamed in `scenes.json`, so update the caller when you rename. A Shortcuts "Run Shell Script" action works on a Mac only.

## Examples

**Example 1: Recording**
```
User: "recording" / "set lights for recording"
→ Control intent
→ bun Tools/Lights.ts scene recording
→ Lights move to the levels saved in the recording scene
```

**Example 2: Back to normal**
```
User: "lights back to normal"
→ Control intent
→ bun Tools/Lights.ts scene normal
→ Each light reports back at the normal scene's levels
```

**Example 3: Tune and persist**
```
User: "key light to 30%" ... "perfect, save this as recording"
→ Control intent
→ bun Tools/Lights.ts set key --intensity 30
→ bun Tools/Lights.ts scene save recording
→ The recording scene now holds the levels the user tuned
```

# SuggestSkills — what should I build next?

A read-only analytics pass over your own work. It answers one question: given what you have actually been doing and where you have been frustrated, is there a recurring problem that deserves its own skill and does not have one yet? It proposes; you decide; `CreateSkill` builds. It has no capability to create or edit a skill, by design.

## Ideal State

- Every proposal on the shortlist traces to recorded evidence (sessions, Errata frustration rows, skill-gap detections) from one tool-built corpus, so a second run over the same window judges the same evidence.
- Gaps hiding under nominally covered topics surface: frustration outweighs topic frequency, and coverage means the discipline is handled, not that a topic shares a keyword.
- The pass stays read-only: no skill is created or edited, and an accepted proposal reaches CreateSkill only as a separate, human-approved step.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **Scan** | "what skills should I build", "skill gap", "suggest skills", "am I missing a skill" | `Intents/Scan.md` |

## Data & Config

The skill reads no config file. `Tools/CollectSignals.ts` takes everything from flags and env vars, and each store resolves flag > env > the first conventional default that exists under the root:

- Root: `--root <dir>`, else `SKILLSCAN_MEMORY_ROOT`, else `$HOME/.claude`.
- Window and cut: `--days <n>` (default 45, 1-3650) and `--max-rating <n>` (default 4, 1-10).
- Stores: `--ratings <dir>` / `SKILLSCAN_RATINGS_FILE` (the Errata ledger directory), `--work <dir>` / `SKILLSCAN_WORK_DIR`, `--skill-gaps <file>` / `SKILLSCAN_SKILL_GAPS_FILE`, `--skills <dir>` / `SKILLSCAN_SKILLS_DIR`, and `--loops <dir>` / `SKILLSCAN_LOOPS_DIR` (opt-in, no default).

The full flag table is in `Intents/Scan.md` § Tool contract.

## Gotchas

- None span intents yet. The collector's gotchas live in `Intents/Scan.md` § Gotchas.

## Examples

**Example 1: routine gap scan**
```
User: "What skills should I build based on my recent work?"
→ Scan intent, last 45 days
→ A ranked shortlist with evidence per proposal, deduplicated against existing skills and intents; nothing is created
```

**Example 2: frustration-led scan**
```
User: "I keep hitting the same wall — am I missing a skill?"
→ Scan intent, frustration store as the lead signal
→ The shortlist includes discipline gaps hiding under topics that look covered
→ User accepts one proposal → handed to CreateSkill as a separate step
```
