# California Wastewater Data Tracking

Pulls California population-level pathogen surveillance from two public sources: CDC's National Wastewater Surveillance System (a viral activity level per treatment plant for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and RSV) and CDPH's sample-level data on the CHHS Open Data Portal (concentrations for every pathogen target CDPH tests). Answers cover California statewide and, when configured, one region of counties.

Clinical case counts miss asymptomatic, unreported and untested infections and trail community spread by days. Wastewater catches everything that enters the sewer regardless of testing behavior, so it leads clinical signals by 4–7 days. Both sources publish on their own schedules; this skill pulls the latest figures each run and turns them into a level and trend you can act on before booking travel or an event.

## Ideal State

- Every answer names the pathogen, the geography it covers (the configured region by name, or California statewide) and the latest data date, so no figure reads as real-time. The date comes from the dataset's own week or sample date.
- A COVID answer gives CDC's own activity level per site and the week-over-week direction; a panel answer covers every pathogen target the CDPH data carries in the past year.
- Figures come from a pull made in this run through `Tools/Wastewater.ts`, with the dataset named so the value can be checked.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **GetCovidData** | "COVID numbers", "COVID status", "COVID data", viral load, activity level, trend before events/travel; default when ambiguous | `Intents/GetCovidData.md` |
| **GetWastewaterData** | "wastewater", "respiratory viruses", "flu", "RSV", "norovirus", multi-pathogen panel | `Intents/GetWastewaterData.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Tools/Wastewater.help.md` | flags, exit codes, what each command reads |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup, the region config, the proof command |

## Data & Config

First-time setup, accounts and a proof command: [Setup.md](Setup.md).

- **Region:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/WastewaterCA/Config.md` (or the file `WASTEWATER_CONFIG` names) holds `- region:`, `- counties:` as `Name FIPS` pairs, and an optional `- rpho region:` for the clinical layer. `bun skills/WastewaterCA/Tools/Wastewater.ts config` prints what a run resolves to.
- **Absent:** with no Config.md every command runs statewide and says so. A county line without a valid `06xxx` FIPS code stops the run with exit 2 rather than silently going statewide.
- No account, key or local dataset; the tool reads public APIs and writes nothing.

## Gotchas

- **CDPH CSV dates are MM/DD/YYYY — never string-sort them.** A lexical compare once reported "Dec 31, 2025" as latest while the data ran into 2026. The tool queries the portal's datastore, where dates are timestamps; parse to real dates in any other path.
- **County columns are FIPS codes in CDPH, names in CDC.** CDPH `county_names` holds codes such as `06067`; CDC `counties_served` holds names. Config.md carries both so each source is matched on its own field.
- **WVAL is not a concentration.** It is CDC's unitless index with pathogen-specific category cut-offs; report CDC's category, never a threshold of your own.
- **The old CDPH statewide COVID file is archived** (last week 2025-08-02). Anything still reading `wastewater.csv` from the Respiratory Virus Weekly Report is reading year-old data.

## Examples

**Example 1: COVID before travel**
```
User: "What are the COVID numbers before my trip?"
→ GetCovidData intent
→ Wastewater.ts covid, then covid --statewide: the week ending date, sites reporting, how many at each CDC level,
  the median site WVAL and its week-over-week direction, region and state side by side
```

**Example 2: Multi-pathogen panel**
```
User: "How are flu and RSV looking in wastewater?"
→ GetWastewaterData intent
→ Wastewater.ts panel: one row per pathogen target with its data date, geography, two-week level against the
  12-month range, trend and sample count
```

**Example 3: Local view with the clinical layer**
```
User: "Is flu actually up around here?"
→ GetWastewaterData intent, with Wastewater.ts covid --pathogen flu and the CHHS dashboard rows for the configured rpho region
→ The regional panel, per-site CDC flu levels, and regional test positivity
```

# Webdesign

Design interfaces using DirectDesign for in-code work, or NativeDesign for artboard variants and design-system sync. Respect existing app tokens and components; redesign only when requested. Both paths share the aesthetic doctrine in `References/FrontendDesignPhilosophy.md` and the same quality loop.

## Ideal State

- Every design lands as working code (or a picked artboard implemented) in the host app's framework, diffed against its existing tokens and components; a full redesign happens only when the user asked for one, and replacing existing UI otherwise is flagged and confirmed first.
- The result looks made for its subject and its host app, never like a generic AI page: a named register, none of the forbidden defaults in `References/FrontendDesignPhilosophy.md`.
- The path fits the ask: DirectDesign for in-code work, NativeDesign for comparing looks or design-system sync, and an ambiguous ask gets both paths offered by name, never routed silently.
- Nothing reaches the principal as a first draft (principal directive, 2026-09-17): before it is shown, the rendered result has an Interceptor capture and an ArtDirection critique that passed the bar, or a reported shortfall.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|--------|---------|------|
| **DirectDesign** (default, bundle `direct`) | in-code UI design or a self-contained page; short ad-hoc design asks, "make a nice design", "do the design yourself", frontend aesthetics, brutalist/editorial/retro/maximalist UI | `Intents/DirectDesign.md` |
| **NativeDesign** (bundle `native`) | artboards, "show me variants", "give me a few directions", "pick a design", mockup, prototype, "claude design", `/design`, `/design-sync`, design-system sync | `Intents/NativeDesign.md` |

DirectDesign fits one pass that lands as code in an existing codebase or as a self-contained page, including when claude.ai access is unavailable. NativeDesign fits when the principal should compare genuinely divergent looks side by side, review visually before implementation, or the job is design-system sync. Illustrations and logos go to Art: brand assets are authored SVG, never generated UI output.

Uncertain routing or the full reference loads bundle `full`. The direct bundle includes the full aesthetic reference and the DirectDesign intent, so its doctrine read is already satisfied; do not fetch the same bytes again. NativeDesign retains its original prerequisites and approvals.

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `References/CompleteGuide.md` | the loader fails, or the `full` bundle: integration-aware operation, preflight, the dated gotchas |
| `References/FrontendDesignPhilosophy.md` | any DirectDesign run or NativeDesign brief: the aesthetic doctrine, registers, type pairs, forbidden defaults |
| `References/InputFormats.md` | writing a design brief, importing a design system, choosing iterate vs restart |
| `References/ClaudeDesignCapabilities.md` | what Claude Design and `/design` can and cannot do, access, known limits |
| `References/SiteLaunch.md` | public-site builds and launch completion |
| `README.md` | the public-facing intro to the skill |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: Interceptor test context for the rendered check, and Claude Design access for NativeDesign |

## Tool contract

Load context with the deterministic loader before executing an intent:
`bun "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/LIFEOS/TOOLS/ContextLoad.ts" Webdesign load BUNDLE`

It returns the selected instructions and their required sections with source hashes; follow every returned requirement. Use `list` to discover sections and bundles, and `search "query"` to search the indexed source; a failed search does not establish absence, so broaden it or load `full`. If the loader fails, read `References/CompleteGuide.md` and the relevant intent directly. Do not proceed with a partial load.

Verification and the quality loop:

- Browser evidence uses Interceptor's `verify` bundle, including all its isolation and safety requirements. An unavailable verifier leaves the result explicitly unverified.
- Capture the rendered page with `Tools/VerifyDesign.ts` or `skills/Interceptor/Tools/Capture.sh`.
- `Skill("ArtDirection")` runs a direction council before new or large work; then the cross-vendor critique panel (`skills/ArtDirection/Tools/Critique.ts`) scores the capture against the rubric and names defects, and this skill iterates on those defects until the bar or reports the shortfall.
- A file handed over through Downloads goes through `skills/ArtDirection/Tools/Deliver.ts`, which refuses without a passing, fresh critique and a Proof receipt.
- Record the principal's verdict with `skills/ArtDirection/Tools/Calibrate.ts`.
- Public-site builds and launch completion also load `References/SiteLaunch.md`; component edits and standalone mockups do not require registration.

## Data & Config

First-time setup (accounts, keys, files to fill in): [Setup.md](Setup.md).

User design preferences (color palette, typography, spacing grid, animation timing, framework defaults, the last shipped sites) live at `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Webdesign/PREFERENCES.md` (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When present they feed every brief, DirectDesign inline, or the NativeDesign artboard brief and design-system project, and bias the register choice without binding it. Never substitute generic defaults for configured preferences. Without preferences, choose freshly each session and rotate registers across runs.

# Workflows

The principal says "I want a new workflow for doing this." This skill turns that into a definition in the definitions home, validated by the `workflow` CLI, and visible on the Workflows page in Pulse.

The CLI is the source of truth: `bun LIFEOS/WORKFLOWS/workflow.ts help --json` lists the commands that exist, their usage strings and exit codes. The format and the system doctrine are in `LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Workflows/WorkflowsSystem.md`. This skill names only commands that `help --json` lists, plus `LIFEOS/WORKFLOWS/engine/schedule-install.ts`, which after a hand edit checks the schedule compiles and the dispatcher is loaded, and is not in that catalog.

## Ideal State

- Every definition passes `workflow validate` (exit 0) before it is reported done, and any deploy, send or pay step declares its `side_effects` and sits under a `human` approval upstream.
- A scheduled or reminder request becomes a `<name>.workflow.yaml` definition with its trigger enabled for the dispatcher, never an issue alone, and shows in `workflow list` and Pulse.
- Every report states the validate-vs-run distinction that applies: `validate` checks shape, `run` executes for real and may spend money or park on a human gate.

## Intent Routing

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Create** | "new workflow", "I want a workflow for", "make a workflow that", "define a workflow" | `Intents/Create.md` |
| **Run** | "run workflow", "run it", "run the workflow", "dry run" | `Intents/Run.md` |
| **Reminder** | "remind me to", "set a reminder", "follow up on", "check back on", any one-off thing due later | `Intents/Reminder.md` |
| **Schedule** | "schedule this", "run this every night", "run it once at", "pause workflow" | `Intents/Schedule.md` |
| **Link** | "link these workflows", "run B after A", "chain workflows", "call a workflow from a workflow" | `Intents/Link.md` |
| **Inspect** | "list workflows", "did it run", "what does this workflow do", "why did it fail" | `Intents/Inspect.md` |

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `Format.md` | authoring reference — load before writing any definition |
| `EvalState.md` | the latest authoring-eval scores (auto-generated, machine-owned) |

## Quick Reference

- Definitions live in `LIFEOS/USER/WORKFLOWS/` as `<name>.workflow.yaml`; the file stem equals `name:`.
- Core commands: `new`, `list`, `validate`, `graph`, `next`, `run`, `runs`, `schedule`, `pause`, `resume`, `link`, `show`, `step`, `put`, `remove`; `help --json` has the full catalog. Every one takes `--json`. Exit 0 success, 1 invalid or failed, 2 usage.
- Every `command` step declares `side_effects` (`[none]` when it touches nothing). A command line that deploys, sends or pays (any `deploy` subcommand or deploy script, a git push, `gmail.ts send`, Relay `send.ts`, `YouTubeUpload` upload, `dd-cli order` and the ordering skill's maintainer-side submit wrapper) must declare the matching effect, or `validate` refuses it.
- Money, deploy and outbound steps need a `human` approval upstream (a human step with the default output, `{approved, note}`). Outbound to the principal only (`recipient: principal`) is exempt. At run time a decline stops the gated step even without a `when`; add `when: { ref: steps.<human>.output.approved, equals: true }` so a decline skips it and the run ends cleanly.
- Local `run` executes all seven step kinds (`RUNNABLE_KINDS` in `engine/runner.ts`). A `human` step parks the run on disk and texts a 👍/👎 approval; `model` and `agent` steps call the OpenAI lanes and cost money; a `workflow` step runs the child as its own ledger run. Only `runs_on: cloud` is refused locally.
- Scratch runs use `LIFEOS_WORKFLOWS_DIR` and `LIFEOS_WORKFLOWS_LEDGER` so they leave the real home and ledger alone.

## Data & Config

Customizations, when present: `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Workflows/` (configRoot is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`).

## Setup

Nothing to configure for authoring. The skill needs `bun` and the `LIFEOS/WORKFLOWS/` engine that ships with LifeOS. Definitions go in `LIFEOS/USER/WORKFLOWS/` (create the folder if it is missing; `LIFEOS_WORKFLOWS_DIR` points the CLI at another one). Status check: `bun LIFEOS/WORKFLOWS/workflow.ts help --json` prints the command catalog and exits 0. Local schedules are evaluated by one launchd job, `com.lifeos.workflows-dispatcher`, so scheduled and reminder workflows that run on this machine need macOS; defining and validating a workflow does not use launchd.

## Gotchas

- **Validator refusals are the design, not obstacles (2026-09-28).** `Step "deploy" declares side effects deploy but no human step is among its ancestors.` is the fix-the-design signal. Add the `human` step; do not remove `side_effects` to pass.
- **An `after` link needs its upstream on disk (2026-09-28).** `after: upstream workflow "no-such-flow" does not exist` appears when the trigger names a workflow that has no definition file yet. Create or fix the upstream first.
- **Lanes are a closed list (2026-09-28).** `Step "summarize" lane must be one of openaiLow, openaiMedium, sol, astra.` A model name in `lane:` fails.
- **Validating is not running (updated 2026-10-09).** `validate` checks shape; `run` executes for real. Every step kind runs locally, so a `model` or `agent` step spends money and a `human` step parks the run until it is answered. Only `runs_on: cloud` is refused by a local run; it runs on its Worker after `workflow deploy`. Say which applies when reporting.
- **A command step with no `side_effects` is refused (2026-10-09).** `Step "x" is a command step and must declare side_effects` means say what it touches; `[none]` is fine for a step that only computes. Declaring less than the command line does, such as a send declared as `[read]`, is refused too.
- **A schedule fires only while the dispatcher is alive (updated 2026-10-24).** No workflow has its own launchd job. One job, `com.lifeos.workflows-dispatcher`, runs `engine/dispatcher.ts serve` under KeepAlive, evaluates every local `schedule`, `interval` and `once` trigger each minute, and starts `after:` and `event` workflows; cloud workflows are scheduled by their own runner. `workflow schedule|pause|resume|put` report `scheduled by com.lifeos.workflows-dispatcher` or `the dispatcher skips it`. After a hand edit of `triggers`, `schedule-install.ts install <name>` only checks the schedule compiles, removes any leftover per-workflow job and makes sure the dispatcher is loaded. Claim a schedule is live only when the definition validates with the trigger enabled, `launchctl list | grep com.lifeos.workflows-dispatcher` shows the dispatcher, `bun LIFEOS/VIGIL/Vigil.ts heartbeat --json` shows its `workflows-dispatcher` row not stale, and `workflow next <name> --json` shows the next fire. The direction is Cloudflare as the clock and the Mac as a worker (Workflows ISA F27).
- **A reminder goes to Vigil as `--class prep`, never by severity (moved from Reminder.md, 2026-10-12).** The class, not the severity, decides Vigil delivery: `prep` is a fixed-rule class, so the next Vigil tick texts it as written. It skips the 72h story hold, quiet hours and the daily text budget, and the editor never rewords or demotes it. An `ops` text can be held, and a held text is never sent later.
- **Clock times follow the principal, not the identity file (2026-10-12).** A clock-time trigger takes its zone from `principalTimezone()`, the current-location zone. A zone copied from the identity file would make "remind me at 9" fire at 06:00 local for a principal travelling three zones west of home. A stored schedule keeps the zone it was written with, so the report names that zone.
- **Reminders and scheduled work are workflows, never issues alone (2026-10-07).** An issue has no schedule and nothing that texts the principal, so a reminder filed only as an issue never fires. Every reminder, follow-up and recurring job is a definition here; an issue may only link to it.
- **Two systems share the word "workflow."** This skill authors definitions with the `workflow` CLI. The inventory of every job LifeOS runs, with missing and orphan reconciliation, is `Workflows.ts`. Route "what is broken or missing" there.
- **A command step gets only PATH, HOME, USER and LOGNAME, plus the names listed under `env:` (2026-09-30; USER and LOGNAME added 2026-10-25 so the claude CLI can find its login).** A variable set on a test run, such as `NODE_ENV=test` meant to stop a send, never reaches the step unless the step declares it, so an undeclared test flag lets a test run send for real. Before testing any step with outbound side effects, declare the test flag under `env:` and confirm the test output shows the skip.
- **No interpolation (2026-09-28).** `"Hello ${name}"` in an argv or prompt is a literal string. Pass values through `with` and `$ref`, and let the command build text from its stdin JSON.

## Examples

**Example 1: create**
```
User: "I want a new workflow that builds the site, waits for my OK, then deploys it"
→ Create.md: workflow new, author build (command) → approve (human) → deploy (command, side_effects: [deploy], when approve said yes)
→ workflow validate exits 0, workflow graph summarised in four lines
→ reports the file path and what runs locally
```

**Example 2: schedule**
```
User: "schedule this to run every morning at 7"
→ Schedule.md: adds a schedule trigger in the principal's current zone (principalTimezone()), validates, prints the next fire times with workflow next
→ workflow schedule writes the trigger and reports scheduled by com.lifeos.workflows-dispatcher; the loaded dispatcher, a fresh heartbeat and workflow next confirm it will fire
```

**Example 3: link**
```
User: "run the report workflow after the export finishes"
→ Link.md: adds an after trigger on the report, checks the export's output schema fits the report's input, validates both, reads the connection class from workflow graph
```

# WriteStory

**Contents:** Ideal State · Intent Routing · The Stance · Tools · Data & Config · Gotchas · Examples

WriteStory is scaffolding for writing fiction. It takes what you already have — a sentence, a folder of notes, a half-drafted chapter — and helps you build the rest of the story one layer at a time, using the systems professional storytellers use on purpose. You bring the creativity; it fills in the pieces you're missing. WriteChapter drafts revisable scenes from your confirmed bible; it never invents the story's spine.

## Ideal State

- Every story element the skill hands back starts from the writer's own material, says whether it was inferred from their seed or offered as a new option, and stands only once the writer ratified or redirected it.
- All seven layers are the destination for every story; the derivation lens the writer's material calls for sets only the order they are reached.
- Each book is a resumable project: its `interview.md` and Story Bible `ISA.md` are read before new work on it and carry what each session confirmed, drafted or changed, so continuity holds across sessions and books.
- Prose comes only from WriteChapter off the confirmed bible, or from Revise on the writer's own draft; either way it was written with the fiction voice model loaded and leaves with its `StoryGate.ts` axes and `StoryJudge.ts` voice line-up shortfall rate attached. The aim is the voice and quality of published fiction, never prose that passes as human.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Interview** | "interview me", "I have notes/an idea for a story", "help me plan a story", "layer my story" | `Intents/Interview.md` |
| **BuildBible** | "build story bible", "create story plan", "map the story" | `Intents/BuildBible.md` |
| **Explore** | "explore ideas", "brainstorm", "I'm stuck", "what if" | `Intents/Explore.md` |
| **WriteChapter** | "write chapter", "write scene", "draft this" | `Intents/WriteChapter.md` |
| **Revise** | "revise", "edit", "improve", "polish" | `Intents/Revise.md` |

The usual path: **Interview** reads what you have and builds the spine with you → **BuildBible** turns it into a Story Bible (a project ISA) → **WriteChapter** drafts off that bible → **Revise** layers and polishes. **Explore** is the idea engine you reach for when a layer is genuinely blank.

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `StoryLayers.md` | defining or checking any of the seven layers: meaning, character change, plot, mystery, world, relationships, prose (BuildBible) |
| `StorrFramework.md` | building character: sacred flaw, theory of control, the dramatic question, status games (Interview, BuildBible) |
| `PressfieldFramework.md` | concept, hook, theme, villain design and the Foolscap one-page method (Interview, BuildBible) |
| `DerivationLenses.md` | choosing the lens that derives the spine: Storr, Cron, Pressfield/Truby, Egri (Interview) |
| `PhasesAndEvents.md` | mapping three-act structure, beats and mandatory events (BuildBible) |
| `StoryStructures.md` | another framework view: Dramatica, Story Grid, Sanderson, Hero's Journey (BuildBible) |
| `AestheticProfiles.md` | setting genre and style (BuildBible, WriteChapter) |
| `AntiCliche.md` | freshness checks and the mechanisms of machine prose (Explore, WriteChapter, Revise) |
| `RhetoricalFigures.md` | the rare moment that wants a figure, from the Forsyth-based catalogue (WriteChapter, Revise) |
| `Critics.md` | the multi-pass prose review (WriteChapter) |
| `Setup.md` | first-time setup: building the fiction voice model (corpus, bands, exemplars) the drafting gate needs |

## The Stance

WriteStory augments a creator and never substitutes for one. The Ideal State's first bullet (start from the writer's material, label it, let them ratify) is the core of it; these rules carry the rest:

- Every derived element is a proposal the writer ratifies, not a fact the system asserts. Label where each one came from: "inferred from your seed" vs. "a new option I'm offering."
- Offer options, not answers: a few directions to choose among, not one rewrite to approve.
- Suggest at the sentence or beat level. Never take over a chapter.
- Anchor to the writer's own voice: their favorites, their samples, their cadence.
- The writer's word always wins. If they redirect, the redirect is the truth.
- Only WriteChapter emits new prose, and only off the writer's confirmed bible, framed as a revisable draft they own; Revise works only on the writer's own draft.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Tools/BuildFictionCorpus.ts` | Splits Project Gutenberg plain-text story collections into per-story `.md` files plus `Corpus.md` manifest. |
| `Tools/BuildVoiceProfile.ts` | Measures every corpus piece and records p10/p50/p90 bands per metric in `VoiceProfile.json`; `--compare <file>` checks a draft against them. |
| `Tools/StoryGate.ts` | Measures draft prose against a human-fiction corpus (dialogue, beat rate, universals) and flags machine-prose drift. |
| `Tools/StoryJudge.ts` | Blind voice line-up against corpus paragraphs (the verdict: does the draft hold up in voice and craft) plus a six-mechanism diagnosis against `Exemplars.md` (advisory); `--detect` adds a which-was-model rate as a diagnostic only. |
| `Tools/VoiceMetrics.ts` | The deterministic metric vector the other tools share; `bun Tools/VoiceMetrics.ts <file> --pretty` prints it for one text. |

## Data & Config

First-time setup (accounts, keys, files to fill in): [Setup.md](Setup.md).

The fiction voice model and every book project are USER data the skill reads at run time; the skill body holds none of it.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Corpus config (Gutenberg ids, authors, anchor) | `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/WriteStory/Corpus/Corpus.json` |
| Per-story corpus files + manifest | `…/WriteStory/Corpus/<slug>.md`, `…/WriteStory/Corpus/Corpus.md` |
| Bands | `…/WriteStory/Corpus/VoiceProfile.json` (from `Tools/BuildVoiceProfile.ts`) and `…/WriteStory/Corpus/StoryProfile.json` (fiction axes, from `StoryGate.ts --build`) |
| Exemplars | `…/WriteStory/Corpus/Exemplars.md` — verbatim passages, loaded before drafting and by the judge |
| History (optional) | `…/WriteStory/History.md` — the install's own incident specifics behind generic lessons here, read on demand |

Build order on a fresh install:

```bash
bun ~/.claude/skills/WriteStory/Tools/BuildFictionCorpus.ts --config <Corpus.json> --fetch
bun ~/.claude/skills/WriteStory/Tools/BuildVoiceProfile.ts --manifest <Corpus.md> --out <VoiceProfile.json>
bun ~/.claude/skills/WriteStory/Tools/StoryGate.ts --build --manifest <Corpus.md> --voice <VoiceProfile.json> --out <StoryProfile.json>
```

Then, per draft: `StoryGate.ts <draft>` (deterministic bands plus the narrator's aside) and `StoryJudge.ts <draft>` (the verdict is a blind voice line-up of the draft's narrative paragraphs against corpus paragraphs, a judge asked which carries the stronger voice and craft, shortfall rate at or under 0.6 to pass; the six-mechanism diagnosis it prints is advisory, and the `--detect` model-detection rate is a diagnostic that never decides a pass). Every tool exits 2 with the build instruction when the model is absent.

Everything above lives under `<configRoot>/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/WriteStory/` (`configRoot` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.claude`). When that directory holds `PREFERENCES.md`, its default genre, aesthetic and voice apply.

Each book is a project under `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/WriteStory/projects/<book-slug>/`:

- `interview.md` — the saved interview results (the spine, the layers, what's confirmed)
- `ISA.md` — the Story Bible as a project ISA: the living plan that tracks what's done and what's left, growing across sessions

## Gotchas

- **The words that fail are ordinary.** A story that passes every banned-word table can still read as machine prose through narrator's asides ('the way everyone reads agreements', 'as anyone would') and rhythm tells; `AntiCliche.md` category 7 is the pass that catches them, and it is a read, never a grep.

## Examples

**Example 1: A writer who already has a lot**
```
User: "I've got a folder of notes for a novel — a few character sketches,
       a rough world, and two draft scenes. Help me build it out."
→ Interview intent
→ interview.md saved: a spine derived from their own notes, every element labeled and ratified, all seven layers marked confirmed / partial / open, the next step left to them
```

**Example 2: Building the full story plan**
```
User: "Build the story bible for my novel"
→ BuildBible intent
→ The project ISA maps all seven layers start to finish, its criteria track done versus remaining, and the gaps still needing a decision are named
```

**Example 3: Writing actual prose**
```
User: "Write chapter 3 based on the story bible"
→ WriteChapter intent
→ A draft of chapter 3's beats the writer owns and revises, reported with its gate axes and a voice line-up shortfall rate at or under 0.6
```

# Writing

Author and revise prose in the principal's voice, audit confirmed AI-writing patterns, and report Pangram scores. The voice itself is data the install supplies: a measured corpus model under the configured voice directory, plus the style guide at `LIFEOS/USER/PRINCIPAL/WRITINGSTYLE.md`. The skill holds the tools that measure, gate and judge against it.

## Ideal State

- Every change to someone's text traces to a confirmed finding or a source span: facts, numbers, quotes, links and the writer's meaning survive, and nothing is added that the source or brief did not supply.
- Prose in the principal's voice aims at the measured corpus model and the anchor piece and clears `VoiceGate.ts` and `VoiceJudge.ts` without being degraded to pass; stripping AI-isms alone never counts as done.
- Every Pangram number comes from a real `PangramScore.ts` run and is reported as a signal with its caveats, never as a pass/fail gate.
- A check that could not run (no config, no key, no Interceptor) is reported as not run, never as passed.

## Intent Routing

| Intent | Trigger | File | Bundle |
|--------|---------|------|--------|
| **Rewrite** (default) | "deai this", "remove AI-isms", "clean up AI writing", "make this sound less like AI", "sound more human", "writing check" | `Intents/Rewrite.md` | `rewrite` |
| **Detect** | "detect", "flag only", "audit only", "just flag", "scan for AI", "detect AI tells", "detect mode" | `Intents/Detect.md` | `detect` |
| **ScoreAI** | "score AI", "test for AI writing", "how AI does this read", "AI detection score", "pangram", "is this AI-detectable" | `Intents/ScoreAI.md` | `score` |
| **WriteAsPrincipal** | "write as me", "write this in my voice", "sound like me", "make it sound like I wrote it", "this doesn't sound like me", "fix the voice", long-form authoring or repair in the principal's voice | `Intents/WriteAsPrincipal.md` | `principal` |
| **Assemble** | "assemble this transcript", "shape these dictated notes", "organize this rough spoken material", "turn this stream of consciousness into prose" | `Intents/Assemble.md` | `assemble` |
| **Preview** | "show me the draft", "preview the article", "open the draft properly", let me see it properly | `Intents/Preview.md` | `preview` |

Uncertain routing, or a request that needs every legacy instruction, loads the `full` bundle (the complete guide and every intent file). Standalone detection with no rewrite intent routes to the public **DetectAI** skill instead; ScoreAI stays here because the publication audit runs it inline.

| File | Read when |
|------|-----------|
| `References/CompleteGuide.md` | the patterns and voice references Rewrite and Detect audit against, the voice config and tool tables, the hard formatting rules, and the skill's gotchas and examples (the bundles load its sections) |
| `Setup.md` | configuring the voice model for an install: config keys, `voice_dir` files, secrets, a proof run |
| `EvalState.md` | checking the `voice-principal` suite's current scores; Assay writes it into your install after the first suite run, so it is absent from a fresh copy |
| `Tools/` | `WritingConfig.ts` flags (`WritingConfig.help.md`); the voice tools are described in `References/CompleteGuide.md` § Tools |

### Loading a bundle

Before executing, load the matching bundle with the deterministic loader:
`bun "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/LIFEOS/TOOLS/ContextLoad.ts" Writing load BUNDLE`

It returns the selected instructions, their mandatory dependencies and source hashes; follow every returned requirement. Required external references and audits still apply. Skill-local paths resolve from the skill root, `LIFEOS/` paths from the install root. An unchanged section already in context needs no second read; after compaction or a source change, reload the relevant bundle.

For bundle reads, set the shell tool output budget to 30000 tokens, and a code-mode wrapper's output budget to 30000 too. A truncation warning anywhere, not only at the `END CONTEXTLOAD` marker, means the load did not succeed.

`list` shows sections and bundles; `search "query"` searches the preserved guide. A failed search does not establish absence: inspect the index, broaden the query, or load `full`. If the loader fails, read `References/CompleteGuide.md` and every relevant intent file directly. Never proceed on a partial load.

## Data & Config

The skill config is `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/Writing/Config.md`. It names the voice directory (`voice_dir`, holding `Corpus.md`, `Exemplars.md`, `PostExemplars.md`, `VoiceProfile.md`, `VoiceProfile.json`), an optional published-content index (`corpus_cli`), the preview browser, and the few example phrases the gate and judge quote. With no config, `VoiceGate.ts` and `VoiceJudge.ts` stop with exit 2 and point at the guide. First-time set-up, field tables and a proof run: [`Setup.md`](Setup.md). The full key and file tables are in `References/CompleteGuide.md` § Data & Config, loaded by the `principal` bundle. `bun Tools/WritingConfig.ts status` reports what is configured.

The env key is `PANGRAM_API_KEY` (ScoreAI only).

## Gotchas

The skill's gotchas live in `References/CompleteGuide.md` § Gotchas, a `required` section in `Context.json` that every bundle loads.

## Examples

```
User: "deai this draft"
→ Rewrite (rewrite bundle)
→ Profile named, findings listed, a minimal-diff rewrite and a clean second-pass audit
```

```
User: "write the intro to this post as me"
→ WriteAsPrincipal (principal bundle)
→ A draft anchored in the principal's published position, with VoiceGate and VoiceJudge exit codes and a reported Pangram score
```

More worked examples live in `References/CompleteGuide.md` § Examples, loaded by the `full` bundle.

# X — Unified X (Twitter) API

**Contents:** Ideal State · Intent Routing · Tools Reference · CLI: xurl · Data & Config · Gotchas · Examples

Handles every X (Twitter) operation through the X API v2 (direct `fetch()`) and the `xurl` CLI: post single tweets, threads and media, publish long-form Articles, search recent tweets, fetch bookmarks, look up user profiles, and read tweets by ID or URL. Other skills delegate their X work here, so the credentials, the auth handling and the OAuth 2.0 token store live in one place; if each skill wired up its own, the secrets would sprawl and the refresh chain would break.

Not for posting the same content to several platforms (`Broadcast`), writing social copy (a copywriting skill), or bulk collection beyond what the X API allows. X reads use the official API or the principal’s own exported data; when X refuses a read, the intent stops and reports it.

## Ideal State

- Every X operation runs through this skill's tools or `xurl` on the auth mode it needs, and every X read goes through `Tools/read.ts`, never a web fetch or browser.
- Nothing reaches the account (a tweet, thread, media post or published Article) without the principal's confirmation, and a post is reported done only after reading it back.
- Posted text and URLs go out exactly as given, measured by X's weighted count; over-limit text is rejected, never cut.
- The OAuth 2.0 grant survives every run: one refresher per grant, and a missing scope or revoked grant ends in a surfaced re-authorization URL, never a guess.

## Tools Reference

All tools are in `~/.claude/skills/X/Tools/` and run with `bun`. Each intent carries the command for its own tool (`post.ts`, `search.ts`, `profile.ts`, `read.ts`, `bookmarks.ts`, and `bookmark-issue.ts` for the sweep's `check`, `create`, `skip` and `audit`); this table holds only the tools no intent owns. Which auth mode each path uses is in Gotchas.

| Tool | Purpose | Usage |
|------|---------|-------|
| `x-client.ts` | Credential loader, token store, auth helpers | Imported by the other tools |
| `media.ts` | Chunked media upload (video/image/GIF) | `bun run media.ts upload clip.mp4` |
| `article.ts` | Long-form X Articles: markdown to `content_state`, draft, publish | `bun run article.ts create --file piece.md --publish` |
| `delete.ts` | Delete tweets by id | `bun run delete.ts <id> [<id> ...]` |
| send gate, video PII gate | What stops a post and how each block is reported | Post intent § Tool contract (`Intents/Post.md`) |

## CLI: xurl

`xurl` is the official X CLI. Use for quick API calls not covered by tools:

```bash
# Quick lookups
xurl /2/users/me
xurl /2/tweets/1234567890

# Search
xurl "/2/tweets/search/recent?query=from:<username>&max_results=10"

# Post (use Tools/post.ts instead for threads)
xurl -X POST /2/tweets -d '{"text":"Hello"}'
```

## Data & Config

Config: `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/X/Config.md` (a fenced `yaml` block choosing the OAuth 2.0 token store: `local`, a 0600 file on this machine that `x-client.ts` refreshes, or `cloudflare-kv`, a KV namespace that another process such as a scheduled Worker refreshes). Setup, field table and first-run proof: `Setup.md`. Without it, reads still work on the bearer token, posting falls back to OAuth 1.0a text-only, and every OAuth 2.0 path (media, Articles, bookmarks, delete) stops with an error naming Setup.md.

The bookmark sweep (PullBookmarks) reads three more things from the same directory and the work-tracking config: the `bookmark_sweep` mapping in that yaml block (issue labels, property label prefix), `PREFERENCES.md` (relevance profile and what counts as an idea), and the repo for idea-issues (`bookmark_sweep.repo`, default the repo in `LIFEOS/USER/WORK/work_repo.json`). Its state lives outside the skill tree in `LIFEOS/MEMORY/STATE/X/` (`bookmarks-state.json`, `bookmark-issues.json`). The caller outside the skill is Pulse's Synapse module, which reads `bookmark-issues.json`; the former scheduled sweep that shelled out to `Tools/bookmark-issue.ts` is retired.

Secrets, all from `~/.claude/.env`, loaded by `Tools/x-client.ts` and never hardcoded (names only):

| Var | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `TWITTER_CLIENT_ID` | OAuth 2.0 client ID (authorize + local refresh) |
| `TWITTER_CLIENT_SECRET` | OAuth 2.0 client secret |
| `X_BEARER_TOKEN` | App-only bearer token (reads) |
| `TWITTER_API_KEY`, `TWITTER_API_KEY_SECRET`, `X_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `X_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET` | Optional OAuth 1.0a text-only posting fallback |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `X_TOKENS_KV_NAMESPACE` | Only for `token_store: cloudflare-kv` |

## Gotchas

- **A published X Article cannot be deleted or edited through the API.** X documents `POST /2/articles/draft` and `POST /2/articles/{id}/publish` and nothing else — no GET, no PATCH, no DELETE. Drafts are free to create and invisible until published, so iterate on drafts and treat `--publish` as one-way. `article.ts` defaults to draft-only for exactly this reason. The X web UI does offer Edit and Delete on a published Article, so a bad publish is recoverable by hand in the browser, not in code.
- **Article `content_state` is DraftJS in snake_case**, not the camelCase DraftJS raw state every online example shows: `inline_style_ranges`, `entity_ranges`, and a flat `entities` array of `{key, value}` rather than an `entityMap` object. Offsets index the stripped text (markers removed). Images, embedded posts, code and dividers are `atomic` blocks whose single-space text is covered entirely by one entity range — a zero-length atomic block is rejected.
- **X's 280-character limit is weighted, not JavaScript `text.length`.** HTTP(S) URLs count as exactly 23 characters and emoji/Unicode follow X weighting in `Tools/TwitterText.ts`. `Tools/post.ts` sends the exact caller input or rejects it (Post intent).
- **`read.ts` returns article and long-tweet text in one call.** It requests `tweet.fields=article,note_tweet`, while X answers WebFetch with 402 and automation browsers are usually logged out, so any other route first only burns time.
- **One refresh chain per grant, ever.** X rotates the refresh token on every refresh and treats reuse of a consumed one as theft, revoking the whole grant until a human re-authorizes. With `token_store: local`, `x-client.ts` is the only refresher: refreshes run behind `<token_file>.lock`, waiters re-read the file instead of replaying a consumed token, and writes are tmp+rename. With `cloudflare-kv`, the external owner refreshes and this client never does. Never call the token endpoint directly with a stored refresh token — always go through `getValidTokens()` — and never point two installs' local stores at the same grant.
- **Three auth modes, not one.** Posting, media, Articles and delete = OAuth 2.0 user context (OAuth 1.0a text-only fallback when no OAuth 2.0 store is configured), reads (search, profiles, tweets) = app-only bearer token, bookmarks = OAuth 2.0 PKCE. A 401 on one path says nothing about the other two.
- **Prefer the OAuth 2.0 store for posting.** OAuth 1.0a portal keys can be revoked or regenerated without notice and then 401 on every post; `post.ts` uses the OAuth 2.0 store whenever one is configured and falls back to OAuth 1.0a only without one. If posting 403s, read the body first: `type: …/spend-cap-reached` means the account's Billing Cycle Cap in the X developer console is hit (every endpoint 403s until the cap is raised or the cycle resets). Otherwise the grant lacks `tweet.write`: re-run `bookmarks.ts authorize`. The consent click is a human's, so surface the URL; if the app grant is still active on the account, authorize completes with no click.
- **Media upload needs its own scope: `media.write`.** Without it `POST /2/media/upload` returns a bare 403 while `/2/tweets` keeps working, which reads as "video posting is broken" rather than "the grant is short a scope". `SCOPES` in `bookmarks.ts` carries it; a grant authorized without it must be re-authorized once.
- **The v2 media endpoints are sub-paths, not `command=` parameters, and X's own chunked-upload doc still describes the retired v1.1 shape.** The working contract is: `POST /2/media/upload/initialize` (**JSON** body: `media_type`, `total_bytes`, `media_category`) → `POST /2/media/upload/{id}/append` (**multipart**: `segment_index`, `media`, segments ≤5MB) → `POST /2/media/upload/{id}/finalize`. Sending `command=INIT` to the base path returns 400 *"Missing media field in JSON"* — the parameter is ignored and the call is read as a simple upload, so the error names the wrong problem. Images ≤5MB skip all of it: one multipart `POST /2/media/upload` with a `media` field.
- **Status is the one call that still speaks the old dialect:** `GET /2/media/upload?media_id=<id>&command=STATUS`. It rejects `media_ids` (the plural that every other v2 endpoint takes) and has no sub-path form. Video/GIF process asynchronously — poll to `succeeded` before attaching, because an unprocessed media_id publishes a tweet with no video and no error. All of this is encoded in `Tools/media.ts`.

## Examples

**Example 1: Read a tweet link**
```
User: "read this: https://x.com/<user>/status/<id>"
→ bun run Tools/read.ts <url> (immediately — no browser attempts)
→ Returns the tweet, plus the full article plain_text when the post carries an X Article
```
`read.ts` takes a status URL or a numeric tweet ID. A bare `x.com/i/article/<id>` link is an article ID, not a tweet ID, and the API has no read-by-article-ID call; use the status URL of the post that carries the article.

**Example 2: Fetch recent bookmarks**
```
User: "show my last 20 X bookmarks"
→ Bookmarks intent: bun run Tools/bookmarks.ts fetch 20
→ Author, text and links per bookmark
```

**Example 3: Bookmark sweep**
```
User: "tb"  (or "just check bookmarks" for quick mode: last 30, MEDIUM skipped)
→ PullBookmarks intent: fetch 50 --json, filter seenIds
→ each new bookmark created-or-skipped inline via bookmark-issue.ts, audit passes, Upgrade report with prior-work tags
```
